## Introduction

Going forward, new issues in the new template at the bottom of this file will go in the '## New format' section only. No more status emojis. Refer to '## Reference' for sort order. Issues in the old format (with status emojis) won't be refactored, but will continue to be worked until moved to closed, canceled, or deferred sections, and emojis updated. (Eventually this will all be moved to nano-git-db anyway. This new template is an intermediate effort to make issues going forward more structured and importable.)

## Issues

- The window doesn't paint while the GPU is busy or short on memory, and stays blank after the load ends
	- ID: 2026100312470535
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Waiting on UAT
		- 20261025: Only the look on b23's own desktop is left, and that has to be done by hand.
	- Stand-in: none (20261028). The blank window was seen only on b23's desktop, through the X11 GL swap and a virtual desktop switch. A headless display doesn't have either, and the 10-03 tries on vm925w never reproduced it.
	- Needs hand testing: Take a dogfood look on b23 with the GPU busy or nearly full. Move to another desktop and back, end the load, and leave the window alone. It should paint on its own. Try it once with "Free resources when idle" on and short idle times too. Started from a terminal with `SILK_IDLEDBG=1`, it prints any refused frame or rebuild.
		- 20261025: The dogfood pool now has build dedvg for Linux and Windows. It was built from dev at a9daddc and has the 10-24 and 10-25 fixes. A window started before the next launch still runs de5r9.
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261003-124705
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100312470540, 2026100418225504
	- Target OS: All
	- Test environment: b23
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Have something else keep the GPU busy, or hold most of its memory.
		- Move to another virtual desktop and back to one with a SilkTerm window.
	- Incorrect behavior:
		- SilkTerm doesn't paint. The only thing visible is the window frame, and other windows and the desktop behind the terminal area.
		- When whatever was using the GPU ends, the blank window is still not repainted. Switching to a different virtual desktop and back repaints it.
	- Expected behavior: The window paints as soon as the GPU can take the work, and never stays blank once the load is gone.
	- Reproduced: No. It was seen on b23 when moving between virtual desktops. It isn't known yet if a window left on screen would also stop painting.
	- Possible cause: A frame that can't get its surface or GPU device under that load is dropped, and nothing tries again until the desktop asks for a redraw.
	- Actual cause:
		- A frame the GPU refused was dropped. The pass that asked for it had already cleared its redraw flag, so nothing asked again until the desktop sent another redraw. That applies to a surface that timed out or went out of date, and on X11 a buffer swap that failed, whose error was ignored.
		- A device that couldn't be built again after the idle release waited for the next key, click, or focus change.
		- Which one happened on b23 isn't known. The terminal window always draws through GL on X11, so the failed swap and the rebuild are the likely ones. It also isn't known whether "Free resources when idle" was on at the time.
	- Notes:
		- Before RC1.
		- 20261003: At filing, b23's GPU had 7.7 GB of its 8 GB in use.
		- 20261003: Settings and the notice window had the same gap, and get the same retry.
		- 20261003: For 2026100312470540: a rebuild refused after the idle release now tries again by itself while the window shows, with a wait that grows to a few seconds.
		- 20261003: Some cases aren't handled. A GL error that arrives after the swap has returned isn't seen. A GPU out of memory while getting a surface on the native path ends the program rather than blanking it, from wgpu's default error handler. wgpu expects a lost surface to be made again, but the code only reconfigures it, so a lost surface would keep being refused. While the GPU keeps timing out, each try can stall the window for about a second inside wgpu.
		- 20261004: Falling back to software rendering when the card can't make a device is filed as 2026100418225504.
	- Actual fix: A refused frame is drawn again after a short wait that doubles up to a couple of seconds, and starts over once a frame gets through. A refused rebuild stays pending and is tried again the same way, with longer waits, while the window shows. A refused frame no longer requests more animation frames, so the wait sets the pace while the GPU refuses frames.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261003: Verified: both new tests fail with the retry taken out and pass with it. The full unit suite, clippy for Linux and Windows, and fmt pass.
		- 20261003: Verified: SilkTerm tried 3 refused rebuilds again at about 0.25, 0.5, and 1 s, and the device came back without any input. SilkTerm backed off 8 refused frames from 16 ms to 2 s, and the window painted again without any input. An idle release and wake with nothing refused still works.
		- 20261003: Tried on vm925w (RTX 2060, 6 GB) with another program keeping the GPU at 100% and using 4.6 GB, then again with memory full until the driver refused more and longer GPU work. The build from before the fix and the fixed build both kept painting: on screen while typed into, after minimize and restore, and after a move to another virtual desktop and back. Neither went blank. Both still showed the right picture 3 and 10 s after the load ended, without any input.
		- 20261003: It was the same with Free resources when idle on and a 5 s idle time. The device was let go and built again under load each time, in about 1 s, and no rebuild was refused. The fixed build logged one refused frame now and then around a minimize, drawn again after 16 ms, never two in a row.
		- 20261003: With Transparency on, which draws through DX12 on Windows, both builds did the same thing: a window restored without focus was let go after the idle time while still on screen, went black when the load ended, and stayed black until typed into. The fix doesn't change this, since a window let go on purpose doesn't need a frame. It wasn't tried without load, because that run hung vm925w and didn't finish.
		- 20261003: Also seen in both builds with Free resources when idle on, under load: after waking, the window sometimes showed only the last character of the prompt instead of the earlier text, until typed into.
		- 20261003: The failed swap path wasn't tested on Windows. The Windows terminal draws through wgpu on Vulkan, or DX12 with Transparency, rather than the X11 GL swap b23 uses. vm925w doesn't have WSL2, so nothing was run through Mesa on the same GPU.
		- 20261003: The black window and the missing text seen in both builds are filed as 2026100319134501 and 2026100319134502.
		- 20261023: Both tests passed in the full run at 2da75a7. The b23 look isn't done yet. No dogfood or desktop runs were made then.
		- 20261025: Both tests passed again in both full runs at e95b81b. The b23 look was moved to the hand testing row, since it needs the visible desktop.
		- 20261026: Both tests passed again in the full run at fab6815.
		- 20261028: Both tests passed again in the full run at 64f3584.
	- Swept: every frame and rebuild site. They're the terminal's acquire and GL swap in `render_with`, called from both `about_to_wait` and the desktop's redraw, the dialog and notice windows' acquire and swap in `DialogWin::render`, and `rebuild_gpu`, which the console-return heal also calls. Nothing else matches `grep -n 'begin_frame\|end_frame\|Gfx::rebuild'`.
	- Branch: gpuload
	- Commit: 8cb6a4d
	- Test case: `a_refused_frame_is_drawn_again_on_a_backoff` (ddf4e) and `a_refused_rebuild_stays_pending_and_is_tried_again` (ddf4f). The GL swap result doesn't have a test, since it needs a real GL context.
	- Note: 20261003, Free resources when idle was on for some of the windows that went blank and off for others. Which ones isn't remembered, so both the frame path and the rebuild path stay suspects.

- When two screens return after screen power sleep or off, SilkTerm seems to reposition itself in between them
	- ID: 2026102807384201
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Waiting on UAT
		- It needs a look on b23, in the hand testing row. The put-back for a window manager that never puts a window back can't be tried on a real desktop here.
	- Needs hand testing: On b23 under xfwm4, with the window on each monitor in turn: let both screens sleep, wake them, and see the window back where it was, at its size.
	- Stand-in: none (20261102). deqx1 already stands in for the window manager's part headless. What's left needs b23's 2 real monitors going to sleep.
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261028-073842
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100907341816
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: b23, xfwm4 4.20
	- Incorrect behavior: When two screens return after screen power sleep or off, SilkTerm seems to reposition itself in between them.
	- Expected behavior: It stays where it was. None of the other ~dozen application windows move, other terminals included.
	- Reproduced: 20261101, headless, with 2 outputs under xfwm4. When the portrait output was turned off, its window was moved onto the landscape one and took that one's size. When it was turned on again, the window stayed there, but an xterm beside it went back.
	- Actual cause: xfwm4 notes where each window was as a monitor goes, and puts it back once the monitor returns, unless the window resized itself in between. SilkTerm took the size kept for the monitor it was herded onto, so xfwm4 left it where it had herded it. Since 2026100907341816 that took place even within a second of the move.
	- Notes:
		- Pre-next-cut.
		- Work first after the CICD issues.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261101: A window herded off a monitor that went dark, or changed, keeps its size and doesn't take any other. It notes the monitor it is on, so a size the user sets there is kept for that one. This reverses 2026100907341816's choice that a herded window takes the other monitor's size. Other windows keep their size too.
		- 20261101: A herd is told from a user's drag by the monitor the window was on at its last look being gone from the layout. Where the window can't say where it is, as on native Wayland, nothing changed.
		- 20261101: Updated an assert, `monwake` (ddq75): "took the landscape size there" is now "kept its size there". In ddq74 the herd step doesn't take a size now.
		- 20261101: Moved back to Queued after the answer to the Check entry. A window can't jump between monitors each time they sleep. The answer asked for 2 things: add a warning to the per-monitor size tip text that the feature can fight the window manager when screens sleep and come back, with unexpected size and placement; and note the window's place and size when a screen goes dark, and if the user didn't move or resize it, put it back there when the screen returns.
		- 20261101: The tip warning is the row's warning mark, as Transparency and the tmux switch have, so it shows on the label too.
		- 20261101: The put-back runs only while per-monitor sizes are taking effect, since only then does SilkTerm move the window off where the window manager leaves it. The window manager gets 2 s first, so xfwm4, which puts windows back itself, is never fought. If the user moved or resized the window while it was herded, it's left alone.
		- 20261101: Updated an assert, `two_rows_warn_and_each_mark_shows_the_rows_tip` (ddp7w): the warned rows were Transparency, the tmux switch, and Free resources when idle, and Per monitor is now among them, on the Window tab.
	- Actual fix: The look after a move takes no monitor size when the monitor the window was on at the last look has left the layout. design.md says so under the per-monitor size. Since the second answer, the Per monitor tip warns that the feature can fight the window manager as screens sleep and wake. A herded window notes where it was and at what size. Once that monitor is back and the window manager has had 2 s, a window not there yet is put back, unless the user moved or resized it since.
	- Swept: every call that resizes the main window. The monitor look is the only one made without the user, apart from the system's own resize for a new scale. The Settings and zoom resizes are the user's. Dialogs are placed once, when they open.
		- 20261101: every place the window notes its place: each look, a size saved, and the window's own resize and the move it can cause. The put-back is skipped while a move is waiting to settle, a button is held, or the window is minimized, maximized, or fullscreen.
	- Verified: 20261101. deqx1 now also runs without a window manager, with the herd made by hand. The window is put back, and left alone when moved or resized while herded. The put-back case fails with the put-back taken out, and the resized case with the forget-on-resize taken out. The xfwm4 cases and monwake pass. The unit tests, clippy for Linux and Windows, fmt, script lints, docs, and test IDs pass.
		- The moved case passes either way here, since under Xwayland a look after a move waits for a sign the drag is over, and that wait leaves the window there too.
		- 20261103: It was run again with xfwm4 gone (2026110315170584). The back case fails with the put-back taken out, and the resized case with the forget-on-resize taken out. The moved case still passes with the forget-on-move taken out, since its look after the move still waits for a sign the drag is over. With nothing taken out, all 19 checks pass.
		- 20261103: The line above was run under an xfwm4 the desktop's session had started again (2026110318260287). It was run again without one on the display (2026110319081175). The back case fails with the put-back taken out, the resized case with the forget-on-resize taken out, and the moved case with the forget-on-move taken out. Each failed only its own case. With nothing taken out, all 20 checks pass.
	- Branch: rnd1101b
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/herdback/run.bash` (deqx1), the window back where it was under xfwm4, and without a window manager. `a_window_herded_off_a_dark_monitor_takes_no_size` (deqwx). `a_herded_window_goes_back_once_its_monitor_is_lit` (der22). `monwake` (ddq75) and ddq74, changed. `two_rows_warn_and_each_mark_shows_the_rows_tip` (ddp7w), changed.
	- Acceptance signoff: Waiting on the b23 look. deqx1 and der22 pass on rnd1101b.

- The monitor sleep and SilkTerm position bug is still there
	- ID: 2026110609500002
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Waiting on UAT
		- It needs a look on b23, in the hand testing row. A headless display can't make an output read disconnected while it stays laid out.
	- Needs hand testing: On b23, with a build from this branch and the window on the landscape monitor: let the screens sleep long enough that the HDMI one drops, wake them, and see the window back where it was, at its size. Started from a terminal with `SILK_MONDBG=1`, the sleep should log `noted` and `herded`, and no `take`.
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261106-095000
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026102807384201
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: b23, xfwm4 4.20, NVIDIA, HDMI landscape and DP portrait
	- Version and build: dogfood of 20261105-150207, which has the earlier fix
	- Reproduced: No. The cause was found from b23's X server log and the GTK and xfwm4 sources.
	- Actual cause:
		- The HDMI monitor drops off as it sleeps. In 7 of 10 sleeps since 10-31 the X server went on laying it out, with its output read as disconnected, and nothing changed the layout until it woke. The other 3 took it out of the layout, which is the case deqx1 tests.
		- GTK skips a disconnected output, so xfwm4 saw one monitor and herded the window off the HDMI one. SilkTerm read its monitors from the server's layout, where the HDMI one was still there, so the herd looked like the user's move. The window took the portrait monitor's size, and xfwm4 forgot where to put it back.
		- The live state file has a `3440x1440_100pct` size without mm. That key comes only from a look while the HDMI output doesn't report a size, which fits a look made while it was asleep.
	- Notes:
		- Pre-next-cut.
		- Need to verify with a fresher build.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261106: On X11 a monitor counts as lit only while one of its outputs isn't read as disconnected, as GTK counts it. When every one reads disconnected, all are believed lit, as GTK then falls back to the whole screen.
	- Actual fix: The X11 monitor list leaves out a monitor whose outputs all read disconnected. That one list feeds both the layout a herd is told by and the monitor a window is on, so the sleep now reads as a herd, which takes no size, and the put-back from 2026102807384201 waits for it. design.md says so under the per-monitor size.
	- Swept: every reader of the server's monitor list, `layout` and the monitor under the window, both through `X11Screen::of`. winit's own list, used where the X server can't be asked, isn't read on X11.
	- Verified: 20261106. deyvh passes, and fails with the disconnected check taken out. deqx1 passes all 20 checks. A probe with the landscape output turned off, as the HDMI one goes, put the window back under xfwm4 before and after.
	- Test case: `a_monitor_whose_cable_reads_disconnected_is_dark` (deyvh). `cicd/tests/herdback/run.bash` (deqx1), unchanged, for the monitor taken out of the layout.
	- Branch: rnd1106
	- Stand-in: none (20261106). Xwayland under headless sway can't report an output as disconnected while it stays laid out, which is b23's usual sleep. deqx1 tests the output being taken out of the layout.

- shcl: `migrate_unstamped` can't say a migration didn't finish
	- ID: 2026100315553545
	- Type: Task
	- Status: Stalled
	- Priority: Low
	- Opened: 20261003-155535
	- Opened by: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100312470546
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- `shcl::migrate_unstamped("notes: ```\nnever closed\n", true)`, at b10c2009 or dev e9e4a6c.
	- Incorrect behavior: it returns `current: false`, `ambiguous: 0`, and `lost: 0`, the same as a migration that finished. A program that then writes its own footer, which is what `migrate_unstamped` is for, puts the Format line inside the raw block, so the file never reads as current. Only the stamped `migrate` shows it, by leaving the Format line off.
	- Expected behavior: `Migration` says when the migration couldn't finish, so the caller can tell without running the stamped call as well.
	- Reproduced: 20261003 on b23, through SilkTerm. A 2.x file with a raw block that never closed was converted in place and no copy of the old file was kept, because the result never read as a newer format.
	- Progress log:
		- It's a missing capability, and a silent wrong answer for a caller that writes its own footer. SilkTerm also calls the stamped `migrate`, in `upgrade` in config.rs, and writes such a file new (2026100312470546).
		- The library also doesn't have a whole-file conversion that keeps a copy of the old file. Only the CLI's `migrate --write` does that, as `config_old_v2.shcl`.
		- It's stalled until a shcl beta has it.
		- 20261007: It's still there, run against shcl dev d7903b73 rather than inferred. The step above still returns `current: false`, `ambiguous: 0`, `lost: 0`, and the stamped `migrate` still shows it only by leaving the Format line off. `Migration` doesn't have a new field. shcl's CLI `migrate` now refuses such a file with exit 7, by the same Format line check. There isn't a 3.0 beta yet, and crates.io still has 2.0.0.
		- shcl dev now has `upgrade()` and `upgrade_file()` for the swap. They convert a whole file with a timestamped backup, close the open raw block, and stamp it. The CLI backup is now `config_backup_<time>_format-v2.shcl` rather than `config_old_v2.shcl`.
		- 20261110: Still there on shcl 3.0.0-beta1 and shcl dev 4901ecac. Filed in shcl's backlog as 2026111014552300.
	- Held for a shcl beta whose `Migration` says when it couldn't finish.

- Wayland: must use the Wayland clipboard, and minimize other X11 features
	- ID: 2026101509024607
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Critical
	- Opened: 20261015-090246
	- Opened by: JC
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: Headless sway on b23, without DISPLAY and with DISPLAY set.
	- Expected behavior: When running on Wayland, must use Wayland clipboard. And also minimize other X11 features in that case.
	- Reproduced: 20261015 on b23, headless sway. Without DISPLAY, `wl-paste` didn't get anything that a copy or OSC 52 sent, and Ctrl+Shift+V and a middle click didn't paste anything from `wl-copy`. With DISPLAY set, SilkTerm opened 2 X connections, one per selection.
	- Actual cause:
		- The clipboard and the primary selection were always the X11 ones on Linux, whatever the window was. A Wayland window didn't have any clipboard without an X server, and with Xwayland, Wayland programs got it only by way of the compositor's bridge.
	- Actual fix: A Wayland window takes the Wayland clipboard and primary on the window's own connection, and doesn't make an X11 context. An X11 window, Xwayland included, still uses the X11 path. The Wayland contexts are let go when the event loop exits, while the connection is still up. It doesn't need any new crates, since copypasta's Wayland side was already built in.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261015: "Minimize other X11 features" was read to mean that on a native Wayland session, SilkTerm doesn't open an X connection unless something doesn't have a Wayland equivalent. The clipboard was the only one left. Everything else already checks the window's handle first.
		- 20261015: Wayland only lets a client set a selection while it has the keyboard. So on Wayland a program's OSC 52 store made while no SilkTerm window has focus is dropped. X11 doesn't have that rule. design.md says so.
		- 20261015: Mesa's Vulkan device select layer can still ask an X server which card is the default, when Wayland can't tell it. That's the driver's own call at device setup rather than SilkTerm's, and wgpu turns on the X11 surface extensions without a way to opt out. It was seen on headless sway with software rendering, but wasn't checked on a real Wayland desktop.
	- Swept:
		- Clipboard: every `Clipboard` user takes the one built in `resumed`, so menus, hotkeys, OSC 52, middle click, copy on select, the tab rename box, and the dialogs all use it.
		- Already gated on an X11 window handle before connecting: the KDE blur hint and the initial window state (app.rs), transient-for and restack (dialog.rs), the work area (dialog.rs), RandR monitor reads, button held, and fullscreen (monitor.rs).
		- Already gated on an X11 event loop: the glutin transparency path and its GLX error hook (gfx.rs), and the MIT-SHM check (main.rs).
		- No connection: `profile.rs` only reads DISPLAY to spot a forwarded display, and `sysfont.rs` asks xfconf over D-Bus.
		- Left: Mesa's device select layer, above. Nothing else connects, per a trace of every connect call with DISPLAY naming a missing display.
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/wlclip/run.bash` (ddzwc), in the pipeline. It checks copy and paste both ways for the clipboard and the primary, without DISPLAY and with it, and checks that no X calls are made. It failed 11 of 13 checks on the old build and passes 13 of 13 on the fix, also with the cores loaded.
	- Verified:
		- 20261015: Checked with real `wl-copy` and `wl-paste` on headless sway, without DISPLAY and with a bogus one. OSC 52 went to both, and `wl-copy` text pasted by Ctrl+Shift+V.
		- 20261015: X11 is unchanged, with the same results before and after. On Xvfb that was OSC 52 to both, then `xclip -o` and a Ctrl+Shift+V paste. On sway's Xwayland with WAYLAND_DISPLAY unset it was OSC 52.
		- 20261015: The gate passed with 1333 tests, and so did clippy on Linux, Windows, and macOS targets.
	- Branch: wlclip
	- Commit: 7add2d9
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, the test fails before and passes after, and the X11 path was checked unchanged.
	- Closed: 20261015-123753

- macOS: the first launch hangs with no window, using more and more memory
	- ID: 2026100114274893
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Needs external testing: A look at the dogfood app from the Dock on b26.
	- Severity: Critical
	- Opened: 20261001-142748
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100113403226
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Test environment: b26, Intel Iris Plus 655, macOS 15.8
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Start SilkTerm on a Mac, here from Spotlight.
	- Incorrect behavior: No window. The Dock shows it running and "Application not responding", and memory climbs until the graphics driver hangs.
	- Expected behavior: The window opens.
	- Reproduced: 20261001 on b26, from Spotlight and from a terminal.
	- Actual cause:
		- The window is created hidden and shown after its first frame. On macOS the graphics layer doesn't give a hidden window any frame at all, so the first frame never came and the window was never shown.
		- Each try had already written its text and other GPU buffers. Returning without a submit left all of them allocated, about 30 MB a second, and the frame was tried again at once.
	- Actual fix:
		- A frame with nothing to draw into still submits, which frees what it wrote.
		- A hidden window that is refused a frame because it isn't visible is shown at once. The startup deadline now applies to a refused frame too.
		- On b26, memory stays flat at about 230 MB and the window opens.
	- Branch: machang
	- Test case: `a_hidden_window_that_cannot_draw_is_shown_anyway` (ddc9r), seen failing without the fix. The memory side doesn't have a unit test, since it needs a GPU.
	- Closed: 20261001-155746

- Scroll scene tmuxclear fails under load, where a clear inside tmux slides
	- ID: 2026110514184921
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261105-141849
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: b23, headless X11
	- Version and build: dev at aeb0fc6
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Load every core, such as 24 `nice -n 19` busy loops.
		- `cicd/tests/scroll/run.bash --only tmuxclear` on a debug build.
	- Incorrect behavior: `FAIL de19r scroll scene tmuxclear (X11), a clear slid: 2 frame(s)`. In the 11-04 16:31 default cicd run it was 5 frames, with the rest of the regression tests running beside it.
	- Expected behavior: Every clear shows at once, under load too.
	- Reproduced: 20261105, 2 of 2 with the cores loaded. It passed 3 of 3 with the box at load 12. It passed in every earlier run log, X11 and Wayland, back to 10-29.
	- Possible cause: It isn't known yet. Either the clear slides when the frames come slowly, which a user on a busy box would see, or the scene's timing doesn't hold up under load. Telling those apart comes first.
	- Actual cause [Bug]:
		- It was the scene's timing. A frame moves a slide on by at most 0.1 s, so with frames a second apart the bursts were still sliding when the clears came. A clear while a big slide still runs slides by design, per 2026101611321631's "Not covered". The failing frames were that leftover slide.
		- With that fixed, there was a second gap. Without a frame between a clear and the next fill, one frame showed the pane scrolled away and then refilled. That is a burst, which slides.
		- To tell them apart, 2 cores were taken by busy loops, with the harness pinned there, which gave a frame about a second. The old scene failed there, with the 4 bursts' slide at its 128-row cap under the clears. Spread across 32 cores, the same load passed twice.
	- Notes:
		- It stopped the 11-04 default cicd run at regression tests, so that run never got to dogfood. Nothing has been dogfooded since 11-01.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261106: It was fixed in the scene rather than in the clear rule. On a box this slow a user who clears while output still slides sees it slide, which is the documented limit. The rule stays out of the way while a big slide runs so a flood in tmux keeps sliding.
		- 20261106: A wait that runs out is a skip rather than a pass or a fail, since the scene never got the screen it tests. altenter does the same.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: After each fill, clear, and mark, the scene waits up to 15 s for a frame drawn since then, at rest, in place of a fixed 0.8 s. A wait that runs out leaves a note, and the analyzer calls that run a skip.
	- Verified: 20261106 on b23, debug build, harness pinned to 2 cores under 6 busy loops. The old scene failed 1 of 1, the first fix failed 2 of 10, and the final scene passed 4 of 4. With a 1 s wait it reported the skip. Quiet runs pass on X11 and Wayland. dcbdt passes. shellcheck, ruff, and `--backlog-run-quick` with all 5 areas pass.
		- Swept: the other scenes on fixed pauses. The `clear` scene under the same load ran past an 85 s limit, so it isn't verified there. It passed in every earlier full run.
	- Branch: rnd1106
	- Closed: 20261106-125200
	- Test case: de19r, scroll scene `tmuxclear` in `cicd/tests/scroll/run.bash`.

- ddydf fails seed 259913750, so the full run stops at step 5: on X11 a drag after a scale change takes no size
	- ID: 2026110915071802
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261109-150718
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026102807384201, 2026110609500002
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Incorrect behavior: The cicd run of 20261109-124912 failed ddydf on seed 259913750. On X11 with per monitor on, output 1 went to scale 1.25, then the window was dragged to output 2. It kept output 1's size, 115x23, where it should have taken output 2's, 122x18. The trace says `herded`, with no `take`.
	- Expected behavior: A drag to another monitor takes that monitor's size, after a scale change on the one it left too.
	- Reproduced: 20261109. The seed fails alone every time, on the host and in the container, with the 11-09 build.
	- Actual cause: A herd was any look where the monitor the window was on last had gone from the layout or changed. A scale change in Xwayland gives that monitor another size at the same place, and an X11 window isn't told about it, so the next look came after the user's drag and read as a herd. A herd doesn't take a size, and its watch waited for the old layout, which never came back. A turned monitor did the same. It came in with the herd change of 11-01.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261109: A monitor counts as gone only when nothing is laid out at its corner any more. A monitor still there at another size was turned, rescaled, or given another mode. A window manager doesn't herd windows off a monitor that is still lit, so a move off it is the user's.
	- Actual fix: `herded` looks for a monitor at the old one's corner rather than for the same rectangle. design.md says so under the per-monitor size.
	- Verified: 20261109. Seed 259913750 passes, and fails on the build from before. The cicd run's seeds from 259913747 and 7 more X11 cases pass. deqwx, changed, and the other herd and monitor unit tests pass. deqx1 (herdback) and ddq75 (monwake) pass.
	- Test case: `a_window_herded_off_a_dark_monitor_takes_no_size` (deqwx), with a turned and a rescaled monitor no longer a herd. `cicd/tests/dpirand/run.py --seed 259913750` (ddydf).
	- Branch: herdscale
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the failing seed and the herd tests pass, and the sleep path is unchanged, since a dark monitor leaves nothing at its corner.
	- Closed: 20261109-150718

- The bash prompt returning after program output slides out downward from under a seam of the higher content, again
	- ID: 2026101415085143
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Needs local test suite run?: The full pipeline, for the Wayland arm of the scroll harness. Unit tests, clippy, and all 13 X11 scenes passed.
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261014-150851
	- Opened by: JC
	- Related IDs: 2026101310563284
	- Target OS: All
	- Incorrect behavior: The bash prompt returning after program output slides out downward from under a seam of the higher content.
	- Expected behavior: The prompt shows up in place.
	- Notes:
		- Pre-next-cut.
		- The bug is back. We need to lock this down with a regression test. Including all similar smooth-scroll-related bugs we've fixed in the past, including nano bounce, nano scroll jumping of static content, muffer's similar bug involving "Jump to bottom" message, etc.
		- Earlier fixes, all in the old-format Done list: "A prompt coming back after a command slides in oddly", "Repeating a command scrolled its output down out from under the prompt above it", "The dreaded 'Nano Bounce Bug' is back", and "Bug: scrolling back in muffer with the mouse wheel made its '1 new message' indicator smear and bounce".
	- Test environment: b23, bash with ble.sh, atuin, and the bundled 2-row prompt in a git repo.
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- In a git repo, so the prompt has 2 rows, `clear`, then run a command whose output leaves the prompt one row above the bottom of the window (`seq 36` in a 43-row window).
		- Run `nano`, and quit it.
	- Reproduced: 20261014 on b23, on dev at b754777, about 1 quit in 4. ble.sh draws the prompt again in place once the minimap column comes back, and that redraw slid down from under the rows above.
	- Actual cause:
		- When ble.sh redraws a prompt already on screen, it erases the old prompt and then makes room with insert- and delete-line, all in one write. The check that a recorded scroll moved something visible looked at the last frame, where the old prompt still showed, so it read the scroll as visible. With the prompt one row above the bottom, the row under it wasn't blank either, so the "room, not a scroll" check didn't catch it.
		- There's a second, rarer path. A relayout drops the frame-old snapshot, and a prompt redraw that gets to a build before a new snapshot slid by default.
		- The flatpak repaint rule (2026101310563284) isn't involved. It's for the output ease, but this is the region slide.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261014: Short and long commands, `clear`, nano, less, `git log`, atuin's Ctrl+R, resizes, and programs turning mouse and focus reports on and off were all tried, on half-empty, full, and full-scrollback screens. Only the in-place redraw near the bottom slid.
		- 20261014: The class has opened and closed several times. Every earlier fix is kept, and each is now pinned by a test that goes red when its own part is broken.
		- 20261014: Already pinned and still passing: the muffer pill smear (`pill` scene and its unit tests), nano's static rows (`nano` scene), and `clear` (`clear` scene). It's waiting on UAT, since it changes what is seen and the case above isn't confirmed as the one reported.
		- Question: does this match what's seen, a prompt sliding down after a program that took the whole window exits? If it shows up some other way, the command and roughly where the prompt was on the screen would settle it.
			- Now I can't reproduce it.
	- Actual fix: a scroll counts as visible only when a row with text in it is now where the scroll put it, or a row with text left. On the normal screen, a recorded scroll without a snapshot to check against shows in place. The alt screen keeps sliding on the record alone, as before.
	- Verified: with real ble.sh and nano, the build before the fix slid 2 times in 8 quits. With the first half of the fix it slid once in 41, which fits the relayout path, though that isn't confirmed. The final build didn't slide in 8 quits. The new scroll scene failed 3 of 3 on the build before the fix and passed 4 of 4 after.
	- Swept: `slide_is_visible` has one caller in the build. `ledger_makes_room` reads the same snapshot but can only stop a slide. The row-print detector compares against `last_rows`, which a relayout leaves at the old width, so nothing matches there.

New replay tests over ble.sh's bytes: ddynt (prompt after output, half-empty and full screens), ddynv (in-place redraw at each height), ddypr (every split of the prompt and the redraw across 2 reads), ddyps (redraw right after a relayout), ddynw (a repeated listing), ddynx (a table redraw snaps while a prompt still eases), ddyny (the nano bounce). - Software rendering crashes on b23 with an X11 BadDrawable error
	- ID: 2026100614510979
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Needs local test suite run?: No
	- Needs external testing: On b23's own desktop, launch with "Always use software rendering" on and open Settings. Then turn it off and on again from Settings and close the dialog. The window draws each time and stays up, with no X error on the command line.
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261006-145109
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100418225504
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: b23, X11
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Run with software rendering on b23. Exact steps not known yet.
	- Incorrect behavior: The program panics. Output on the command line:
		~~~text
		SilkTerm: renderer = llvmpipe (LLVM 19.1.7, 256 bits) [Vulkan / Cpu] alpha = premultiplied
		[2026-10-06T20:35:24Z ERROR winit::platform_impl::linux] X11 error: XError {
		        description: "BadDrawable (invalid Pixmap or Window parameter)",
		        error_code: 9,
		        request_code: 149,
		        minor_code: 4,
		    }
		(the same error twice more)
		thread 'main' (313787) panicked at /cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/winit-0.30.13/src/platform_impl/linux/x11/window.rs:1276:37:
		Failed to call XResizeWindow: XError { description: "BadDrawable (invalid Pixmap or Window parameter)", error_code: 9, request_code: 149, minor_code: 4 }
		~~~
	- Expected behavior: Software rendering runs like the card does, only slower.
	- Reproduced: Yes, at launch with the setting on and when it is turned on while running, with the same errors, on an X server that can't make shared pixmaps, as b23's can't.
	- Possible cause: Request 149 is DRI3 on b23's X server, and minor 4 is FenceFromFD, which lavapipe's X11 present path sends. So lavapipe presented to a window the server no longer knew. winit only reports a queued X error at its next checked call, so XResizeWindow got the blame. A window swapped or rebuilt under a live surface would fit.
	- Actual cause: Mesa's software Vulkan presents on X11 through shared memory pixmaps whenever the server has DRI3, without asking whether the server can make them. b23's X server on the NVIDIA driver can't. Each one is refused silently, the fence made on it then fails, and winit dies at its next X call. Every software window and dialog was hit, so the launch and the switch failed alike.
	- Actual fix: At launch on such a server, the program turns Mesa's shared memory path off (`MESA_VK_WSI_DEBUG=noshm`), so software frames get to the window as plain images. It's X11 only, and only when the server says it doesn't have shared pixmaps. Shells started from SilkTerm inherit the variable, which spares a software Vulkan program run there the same crash.
	- Note: The checks on 2026-10-04 passed because those X servers can make shared pixmaps.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261006: Shells inheriting the variable is OK as long as it doesn't have any major drawbacks. None were found. Only Mesa's software Vulkan reads it, and only on an X server where the shared path fails anyway. Frames there are copied as plain images, a bit slower on a big window.
	- Sweep: every software device that draws to an X window.
	- Swept: the main window at launch, after a switch, and after an idle rebuild, plus the dialogs' kept context and the one a dialog builds without it. All read the one process setting, which is in place before any of them exists. Windows and macOS don't have that path.
	- Branch: swcrash
	- Commit: 7e50f19
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/swnoshm/run.bash` (ddkex), which fails on the old build at launch and on the switch and passes with the fix. Unit test `no_shared_pixmaps_turns_mesa_shm_off` (ddkew).
	- Verified: The window test both ways, the Linux unit tests, and clippy for Linux, Windows, and macOS.
	- Notes:
		- Before RC1.
	- Closed: 20261015-121132

- A software rendering launch crashes now and then inside the Vulkan loader
	- ID: 2026100720280486
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Needs local test suite run?: No
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261007-202804
	- Opened by: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100614510979
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: b23, the debug build, headless sway's Xwayland behind the no-shared-pixmaps proxy
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Run `cicd/tests/swnoshm/run.bash` a few times. Its first case launches with software rendering on.
	- Incorrect behavior: the program dies of SIGSEGV within about a second of launch, before a window comes up. The kernel log puts both crashes in `libvulkan.so.1.4.309` at almost the same offset, 0x2d066 and 0x2d06e. The faulting address in one crash was 0x6472616373, which is ASCII text read as a pointer.
	- Expected behavior: a software launch comes up every time.
	- Reproduced: 20261007, in 1 of 3 runs of the test alone at load 7, and once in the full pipeline at 7a032c5. No core was kept. The case that switches to software while running passed every time.
	- Possible cause: it isn't known. The same spot both times points away from host noise. Debug builds turn on Vulkan validation through `InstanceFlags::default()`, and the dialogs' GPU context is built on a worker thread, so 2 instances made at once in the loader is one suspect. Whether a release build crashes too isn't known.
	- Actual cause: The Vulkan loader on Debian 13 (1.4.309) has a threading bug. To find which device a call is for, it walks every instance's list of drivers, under a different lock than the one held while those lists change. Debug builds name every object they make, and each name does that walk. The dialogs' warm-up makes its own instance on another thread right after the window shows, and listing its adapters unloads the drivers that don't have any. A name given on the window thread at that moment read a list entry that had just been freed. Loader 1.4.350 fixes it upstream.
	- Actual fix: Every thread that calls into the loader takes one lock while it does. The warm-up holds it for its whole build. The window thread holds it through each event-loop callback, but only while a window draws on Vulkan, which means software rendering or Wayland. A window on GL never waits. A wait on the warm-up lets go of the lock first, and the program lets a warm-up finish before it exits.
	- Note: Release builds don't name anything, so far less of what they do takes that walk. Making a swapchain or a device still does. About 2400 devices made beside 600 warm-up builds didn't crash, but the fix applies to them anyway.
	- Note: The cost is one wait, right after a window on Vulkan shows and after each idle rebuild, if the window has work while the warm-up builds. On an optimized build on b23 it's about 130 ms with the card on Wayland, 35 ms in software, and 0 with the card on X11.
	- Against: the kept dialog context (2026100418225505, `WARM_DIALOG_GPU`). It's still kept and still built on a worker thread, but a window on Vulkan can now wait for that build once.
	- Sweep: every thread that calls into wgpu, and every wait on one.
	- Swept: Only the window thread and the warm-up use wgpu. No other spawned thread does. The 2 waits on the warm-up, opening a dialog and letting the device go, both let go of the lock. The unit tests that make devices take it as well, since they run side by side. `--about` runs before any thread starts.
	- Branch: vkload
	- Commit: 7d492b7
	- Test case: `a_warm_up_never_overlaps_what_the_window_draws` (ddp6r) crashed 3 of 3 runs with the warm-up's hold taken out and passes with it. `a_loader_hold_nests_and_lets_go_for_a_wait` (ddp6s). `only_a_window_on_vulkan_holds_the_loader_through_its_callbacks` (ddp72) fails when every window holds.
	- Verified: 20261008, the full unit suite, clippy for Linux, Windows, and macOS, `cicd/tests/swnoshm/run.bash` 3 times, and 20 more software launches without a crash. Before the fix the same launches crashed 1 in 15 at load 18, at the filed spot.
	- Notes:
		- 20261007: The validation layer also reports an overlapping `vkCmdCopyBufferToImage` on the minimap and wallpaper textures, in passing runs too.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, and the 3 tests fail without the fix. On dev at 07f3f6a the gate passed and `cicd/tests/swnoshm/run.bash` passed 4 runs in a row at load 6 to 15.
	- Closed: 20261013-105632

- The curated default font list got replaced by just its first font
	- ID: 2026100913394946
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261009-133949
	- Opened by: JC
	- Related IDs: 2026100907341818, 2026101009220980
	- Target OS: All
	- Incorrect behavior: The default list of fonts I had carefully curated got replaced by just the first one.
	- Expected behavior: Bring the full list back.
	- Notes:
		- Before RC1.
		- From the Settings UI update.
	- Reproduced: 20261013 on b23. With "Use system font" on, Family showed "Monaspace Argon" alone, and turning Face off kept and saved that one name. Test ddwhp failed before the fix.
	- Actual cause:
		- The built-in list was never cut. Since 10-09, Family's automatic value is the desktop's monospace font, and on b23 the desktop's font is Monaspace Argon, which is also the list's first entry. So the box showed one name.
		- Turning the switch off keeps what the box shows, so it saved that one name as the family.
		- The live config on b23 wasn't cut. The 10-09 launch only commented out its family line, which had the full list and still reads the same.
	- Actual fix: When it follows the desktop, Family is now the desktop's font followed by the built-in list, each name once. On b23 that is the old list exactly, and turning the switch off keeps and saves all of it.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261013: The automatic list is the desktop's font and then the built-in list, rather than the desktop's font and a list set by hand. A list set by hand is set aside while the switch is on, as for every other switch.
		- 20261013: There's no launch repair for a file with only `family: "Monaspace Argon"`. It isn't the old default, it can't be told apart from a pick made by hand, and it renders the same while that font is installed. No such file was found. b23's is fine, Windows doesn't name a desktop font, and a Mac names one only when somebody picked it, so the bug couldn't happen on the Windows boxes or b26.
	- Swept:
		- Every reader of the rule goes through `system_font_family` in fields.rs.
		- The font search in text.rs takes the longer list as it is, since it drops repeats.
		- The size rule gives one number, so it doesn't have a list to lose.
		- The glossary, the Unicode design doc, and code comments that said the automatic family is the desktop's font alone.
	- Verified: the unit suite, the merge gate (fmt, clippy, and tests), and the test ID, doc, TOC, and table checks.
	- Not checked: a real window, Windows, and macOS.
	- Branch: fontlist
	- Commit: 5f3623b
	- Test case: ddwhp `the_family_keeps_the_whole_list_when_the_switch_goes_off` failed before the fix and passes after. ddwhq `the_desktop_s_font_leads_the_built_in_list` pins the list on any desktop. ddqa4's family assertion was changed to the new rule.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, the test failed before the fix and passes after, and the list on b23 is the old list exactly. The gate passed on dev at 07f3f6a.
	- Closed: 20261013-105632

- vm925w: The silkterm launcher in the taskbar doesn't work.
	- ID: 2026100710173170
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261007-101731
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100314050020
	- Target OS: Windows
	- Test environment: vm925w
	- Incorrect behavior: A minimized cmd window shows briefly, then disappears.
		- But the same command it runs, run by hand in a cmd window, works.
	- Notes:
		- Before RC1.
	- Reproduced: 20261007 on vm925w, with a click on the taskbar pin. The minimized cmd window ran `runterm.cmd`, started no pwsh, and exited 1.
	- Actual cause: The PATH that the taskbar hands to what it starts had lost PowerShell 7's folder, and `runterm.cmd` looked for pwsh on PATH only.
		- Explorer rebuilds its PATH when a program announces an environment change, and cuts it at 4095 characters. vm925w's machine PATH is 4142 once expanded, so the cut falls right before pwsh's folder and drops the whole user PATH too.
		- A console opened before that, or a Windows Terminal tab, still has the whole PATH. So the same command worked by hand.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261007: The pin runs the live `runterm.cmd` under Dropbox, which is the repo's 01ed285, and that runs the live `n8runterm.ps1`, the repo's 4f2fa50 from 10-01. Neither has the 10-06 launcher changes, so fastlaunch and StrictMode are ruled out. `runterm.log` didn't have a line for any failed click.
		- 20261007: The taskbar's own PATH was exactly 4095 characters and ended in `C:\Pr`. A fresh environment built from the same registry is whole.
		- 20261007: install.ps1 announces an environment change, and its tests ran on vm925w at 09:04 that morning. Any installer does the same, so that's the likely trigger, but it isn't proven.
	- Actual fix: `runterm.cmd` looks for pwsh on PATH, then where its installer records it (App Paths), then its default folder, then the Store's alias. The machine install comes before the Store's, so a cut PATH gets the same pwsh as a whole one.
	- Verified: The new test on vm925w failed 3 checks on the old `runterm.cmd` and passed on the new one. With `runterm.cmd` run in the taskbar's own environment on vm925w, the old one exited 1 and didn't start anything, and the new one opened a SilkTerm window. ps-lint passed on the changed scripts.
	- Swept: `git grep` for pwsh found by name over install.ps1, `utility/`, and the cmd files. `runterm.cmd` was the only launch path that needed PATH. `n8runterm.ps1` relaunches itself by its own full path. The elevated relaunch gets a fresh environment, so the terminal it opens had the whole PATH.
	- Note: The pin runs the live copies outside the repo, so on vm925w it keeps failing until the live `runterm.cmd` is replaced with this one. The live `n8runterm.ps1` is older than the repo's too. Signing out and back in gives the taskbar a whole PATH again, until the next cut.
	- Branch: pinpath
	- Commit: 2f692b7
	- Test case: New Windows test `cicd/tests/launcher/wrapper.ps1` (ddmj2), run by `cicd-win.ps1` in stage 3. It runs `runterm.cmd` with every folder that has pwsh.exe taken off PATH, and checks that the launcher still starts, under the same PowerShell 7 a whole PATH gives.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, the test failed before the fix and passes after, and the fix worked in the taskbar's own environment.
	- Closed: 20261007-111713

	- ID: 2026100114435547
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done

The whole dialog stays below the menu bar and above the Dock, buttons in view, centered over the terminal where it fits. Try it again with the Dock on the side and hidden. About opens over the terminal too.
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261001-144356
	- Opened by: JC
	- Closed: 20261006-140904
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Test environment: b26, Intel Iris Plus 655, macOS 15.8
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Open Settings.
	- Incorrect behavior: The dialog is nearly the height of the screen, and it is placed so the buttons sit below the bottom edge.
	- Expected behavior: The dialog is a sensible size and fits on the screen, buttons included.
	- Reproduced: No. The Mac was busy, so the cause was found by reading the code and pinned by a test.
	- Actual cause:
		- macOS didn't have a work-area read, so the height cap was the whole display less a title bar, and nothing placed the dialog.
		- macOS centers a new window at its first, smaller size, and a window that grows keeps its bottom edge. A dialog that tall was then pushed down from under the menu bar, and its buttons went off the bottom.
		- Text a third too big made the natural height taller still (2026100114435561).
	- Actual fix:
		- The cap comes off the screen's visible frame, which leaves out the menu bar and the Dock.
		- The dialog is centered over the terminal and moved onto that area, the same as on Windows. The placement is shared, so on Windows a dialog over a terminal on a monitor left of or above the primary now stays there instead of moving to the primary.
	- Swept: Both callers of the work area, the size caps and the placement. About uses the same placement.
	- Test case: `a_mac_dialog_fits_between_the_menu_bar_and_the_dock` (ddcdz) and `a_dialog_stays_on_a_monitor_left_of_the_primary` (ddce0). The first fails with the old cap, the second with the old clamp.
	- Verified: The unit tests on Linux, and clippy for Linux, Windows, and macOS.

	- Closed:

- A shell is listed twice by name, with a different command each time
	- ID: 2026100408214203
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Needs external testing: On b26, a scan into a new throwaway config (`--config`). The Tabs menu and the Shell tab should show "Bash 3.2.57" and "Bash 5.x" with their own commands, and no plain "Bash" twice. Nothing should flash on screen while the versions are asked. The live config's list shouldn't change.
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261004-082142
	- Closed: 20261006-140839
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100408214202
	- Target OS: All
	- Test environment: b26
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- On macOS, have Bash installed at both /usr/local/bin/bash and /bin/bash.
		- Let the shell scan run.
	- Incorrect behavior: "Bash" shows up twice, once for /usr/local/bin/bash, and again lower down for /bin/bash.
	- Expected behavior:
		- Fix it in general, not just for macOS.
		- If a shell is listed twice by Name but with a different Command:
			- If one is a symlink of the other, list the shortest path, whether it is the symlink or the real file.
			- If the shell version is the same, only list the one with the shortest path.
			- If the shell version is different, add the version to the Name, without extra build info.
				- E.g. "Bash 3.2.1", "Bash 5.1.0", etc.
	- Notes:
		- Before RC1.
		- 20261004: On a Mac, /bin/bash is Apple's old 3.2, and /usr/local/bin/bash is usually a newer one from Homebrew, so this case likely gets the version names.
		- 20261004: A change to the scan doesn't change a list already saved.
		- 20261004: Duplicates already in a saved list are left alone, and the fix applies to new finds only. A scan only adds shells and switches off missing ones, so a detection fix doesn't apply to an existing list.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261004: Leave duplicates already in a saved list alone. The fix applies to new finds only.
	- Reproduced: 20261004, b23, with the Mac's 2 bashes stood in. The scan offered "Bash" twice. Tests ddg73, ddg74, ddg75, and ddg76 failed before the fix.
	- Actual cause:
		- The scan keeps 2 different files as 2 shells, which is right, but names both after the program. On a Mac, PATH finds Homebrew's bash and /etc/shells lists Apple's /bin/bash.
		- Where one file was found 2 ways, the scan kept the first spelling it met rather than the shortest.
	- Actual fix:
		- A file found 2 ways is offered at the shorter path.
		- When 2 finds with one name are different files, each is asked its version. With the same version there's one entry, at the shorter path, in the place of the first found, so a login shell stays at the top. With different versions, each name gets its version.
		- The version is the first dotted number the shell prints for `--version`, without build info. Only a shared name is asked. Each ask is stopped after 2 seconds, and a shell that doesn't respond keeps its plain name.
		- The login shell's "(no rc)" twin follows its shell's path and name, such as "Bash 5.2.37 (no rc)".
		- A number already at the end of a name grows rather than doubling, so "Python 3" becomes "Python 3.12.1".
	- Swept: the scan is the one place shells are found. `merge` and the saved list are unchanged.
	- Verified: unit tests, and clippy for Linux, macOS, and Windows. There's no real Mac scan yet.
	- Branch: shname
	- Commit: 07ad847
	- Test case: ddg73 `two_versions_of_one_shell_each_show_their_version`, ddg74 `one_version_installed_twice_is_offered_once_at_the_shorter_path`, ddg75 `a_shell_that_will_not_say_its_version_keeps_its_name`, ddg76 `a_shell_and_its_link_are_offered_at_the_shorter_path`, ddg77 `a_version_goes_into_a_name_the_way_a_person_would_write_it`, ddg78 `the_version_probe_gives_up_on_a_program_that_never_answers`. The first 4 failed before the fix.

- macOS: a window opened with Command+N is smaller, and its size is the one remembered
	- ID: 2026100514211602
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261005-142116
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100114435600, 2026100408214201
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Test environment: b26
	- Requirements:
		- Before RC1.
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Open a window with Command+N.
		- Close the new window, then the one it was opened from.
		- Launch SilkTerm again.
	- Incorrect behavior:
		- The new window opens smaller than the one it was opened from.
		- The next launch opens at that smaller size.
	- Expected behavior: A new window opens at the size a fresh launch would use. Closing windows doesn't shrink the remembered size unless one of them was resized.
	- Reproduced: 20261005 on b26. A window opened at a remembered 140x22, and nobody resized it, yet within a second the file said 116x35. A window opened from it with New window came up at 116x35, which is also what the next launch reads.
	- Possible cause:
		- Each window is its own process, and the new one reads the remembered size for the monitor it thinks it opens on (`MonitorId::of_new_window`). macOS may report that differently for a window started from another one.
		- A size is saved at close only if the window changed size (`flush_window_size`). If the new window's first size counts as a change, it saves the small size, and the first window, never resized, doesn't save anything.
	- Actual cause:
		- Neither possible cause was right. Both windows looked up the same monitor, and the first one's size wasn't the one saved.
		- On macOS winit hands over the resize from the window's creation, at the default 1000x640 points, after the first frame. A resize counts as the user's from the first frame on, so the default window's grid was saved. The real size came next, inside the wait that skips the system's resizes after a scale change, so nothing put it back.
		- So every macOS launch saved the default grid, 116x35 at b26's font, while the window itself showed the remembered size. A new window, or the next launch, then opened at 116x35.
	- Actual fix: A resize counts only when it is the size the window has at that moment, so a late one is skipped. On every platform a current resize has that size.
	- Swept: every path that saves a size. The window's resize had the fault. A font zoom takes the window's own size, and a move to another monitor asks for its size inside the skip. A resize to no area, which a minimized window on Windows sends, saved 1x1. That was filed and fixed as 2026100517535924.
	- Verified:
		- b26: with the fix, the item's steps at 140x22 kept 140x22 in the file, and the new window and the next launch opened at the first window's size. A resize was still saved, and the next window followed it.
		- Linux X11: there was no fault before the fix either. Ctrl+Shift+N opened at the first window's size, and nothing was saved. With the fix, resizes are still saved.
		- Linux Wayland, with the fix: a launch doesn't save anything, and a resize is saved. It wasn't run before the fix.
		- Windows, vm925w: there was no fault for New window or a launch before the fix either.
	- Note: It still needs a check by hand on b26 of the Command+N key and a resize with the mouse. The New window menu action and a resize were checked.
	- Note: b26's dogfood build is from 20261003, so it keeps saving 116x35 until the pool has a newer build. Its config has 116x35 from that build.
	- Branch: cmdnsize
	- Commit: f442520
	- Test case: `a_resize_the_window_has_moved_past_is_not_saved` (ddj41), failing on the old code. The X11 window test `cicd/tests/startsize/run.bash` (ddg81) now checks that a launch doesn't save a size, and the Windows scenario `newwin` (ddj42) checks New window, a launch, and a minimize.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced on b26, the item's steps pass there with the fix, and Linux, Wayland, and Windows were checked.
	- Closed: 20261005-175359

- Light mode: the scrim is much too strong next to dark mode
	- ID: 2026100513581811
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261005-135818
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: All
	- Requirements:
		- Before RC1.
	- Incorrect behavior: Over a wallpaper, the light-mode scrim reads much stronger than the dark-mode one at the same setting.
	- Expected behavior: The two modes look about as strong as each other.
	- Notes:
		- 20261005: It came from the look at the old-format cursor plate item.
	- Reproduced: 20261005 on b23. It was measured as how far the halo and outline move pixels from the same scene drawn without them, mean sRGB levels per pixel over a screenful of text, dark against light. The built-in wallpaper gave 6.6 against 20.1, a dark photo 3.8 against 13.0, and a near-black photo 2.2 against 13.8. So light mode was 3 to 6 times as strong. In Oklab lightness the two looked about even, but sRGB levels are what the visibility work matched and what the eye agreed with.
	- Actual cause:
		- Light mode scaled the halo by one gain, matched at half the halo over an average picture. sRGB's curve makes dark mode's halo build slowly and light mode's fast, so the faint tail showed far more in light mode.
		- Light mode draws a picture, dark parts most of all, much further from the paper than dark mode draws it from black. A gain matched to an average picture couldn't follow that.
		- The 1 px outline was never scaled at all, so in light mode it moved pixels by up to 119 levels.
	- Actual fix: Light mode redraws every halo alpha, the outline included, off a curve solved per picture. The curve makes the halo move the picture toward the background as far, in sRGB levels a channel at a time and on average over the picture, as dark mode's halo moves dark mode's. The wallpaper summary now stores 16 quantiles of each channel for this. Dark mode, and light mode without a wallpaper, are drawn as before. After the fix it's built-in 9.5, dark photo 4.9, and near-black photo 2.6, against dark mode's 6.6, 3.8, and 2.2, which is 1.2 to 1.4 times. The rest is the picture under the text not being the picture's average, which the composite can't see.
	- Decisions:
		- The old floor of a quarter of the asked alpha is gone. It kept the tail up, which is where the excess was. The text's own contrast is what keeps it readable, and light-mode text is darker now (2026100513581810).
		- It's matched in sRGB levels rather than Oklab, as the wallpaper visibility work was.
	- Verified: dark mode draws exactly the pixels it drew before, in all 4 themes adn without a wallpaper. The full unit suite passes.
	- Swept: the composite has one output, the union of halo and outline, and the match runs there, so the cursor's halo and outline go through it too. `halo_gain` had one caller. The cursor plate has its own light-mode alpha and isn't part of the scrim.
	- Branch: lightink
	- Commit: b36853d
	- Test case: `the_halo_covers_the_same_ground_in_both_modes` (dcx42), now at every alpha and over gray and strongly colored pictures, and `the_halo_follows_the_picture_it_sits_on` (ddj1n), both failing on the old single gain. `only_a_matched_halo_is_redrawn` (ddj1r) keeps dark mode out of the match, `the_scrim_shader_compiles` (ddj1q) validates the shader without a GPU, `the_matched_halo_only_ever_grows_with_what_was_asked` (ddj1p), and `the_memo_never_hands_back_a_stale_halo` (ddj1t).
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: measured before and after in both modes, dark mode pixel-identical, tests pass.
	- Closed: 20261005-171619

- Linux: the window opens at one size, then jumps to another
	- ID: 2026100408214201
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Needs external testing: A look on the b23 desktop with one monitor and with two, and with Remember maximized on.
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261004-082142
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: b23
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Start SilkTerm.
	- Incorrect behavior: The window shows at one size, then resizes itself.
	- Expected behavior: The window is already at its final size when it first shows.
	- Possible cause: This was fixed on 20260720 under Done, in "On open, when it becomes visible, it should already be at its final size". The per-monitor size work on 20261003 (2026100114435600) changed how the starting size is chosen, so it's the first suspect. It wasn't checked.
	- Reproduced: 20261004 on b23, under xfwm4, and with 2 monitors. Opened from the second monitor, the window was sized for the first and changed size about a second after it showed. With Remember maximized on, or `--fullscreen`, it showed at its restored size and then grew.
	- Actual cause:
		- The launch chose the monitor by where the hidden window was, which is always the top-left corner. The window manager then opened it under the pointer, and the check after a move gave it that monitor's size. It came from `permon`.
		- Maximized (from `maxdlg`) and fullscreen were only asked for after the window was shown, and a window manager ignores the request before that. So the window showed at its restored size first.
	- Notes:
		- Before RC1.
		- Note: 20261004, with one monitor and Remember maximized off, neither cause applies. A jump seen that way is a third cause.
		- Note: 20261004, b23 has 2 monitors, and the one at the top-left corner isn't the main one. Remember maximized is on in its config. So both causes apply there.
	- Actual fix:
		- The launch takes the monitor under the pointer, where xfwm4 opens a window that doesn't ask for a position. A window manager that puts it elsewhere still gets the size change after it shows.
		- On X11 the maximized and fullscreen states are written on the window right before it's shown, and the window manager reads them as it maps it.
		- That isn't done on Wayland, where a window learns its monitor only once it's shown.
	- Swept: everything that sizes the window or sets its state before it shows. The launch size and the monitor lookup (the one taken after a move still goes by the window), maximize, and `--fullscreen`, which had the same fault. The Settings dialog doesn't set any window state.
	- Verified: with 2 monitors, the old build changed size after showing in 2 of 2 launches and the fix in 0 of 2. Maximized, the old build showed at the restored size first in 10 of 10 launches and the fix in 0 of 10. `--fullscreen`, 3 of 3 against 0 of 5. Unit tests and clippy pass.
	- Branch: sizejump
	- Commit: 527a597
	- Test case: `a_window_not_shown_yet_opens_on_the_monitor_under_the_pointer` (ddg7r), seen to fail with the pointer ignored. `cicd/tests/startsize/run.bash` (ddg81): a remembered size, 3 maximized launches, and `--fullscreen` must each show once, at one size. On the old code the fullscreen case fails every run and the maximized one in most. The 2-monitor case isn't in it, since its display has one monitor.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: both causes reproduced, fixed, and pinned by tests that fail on the old code. The real desktop still needs a look.
	- Closed: 20261004-094713

- macOS: "Bash (no rc)" shows in the menu as "Bash", so "Bash" is listed twice
	- ID: 2026100408214202
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261004-082142
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Test environment: b26
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Open the menu that lists the shells.
	- Incorrect behavior: "Bash (no rc)" shows as "Bash". Renaming it to "Bash no rc" makes it show right.
	- Expected behavior: The menu shows the shell's full name.
	- Possible cause: On macOS, `plain_label` in app.rs takes off anything in parentheses at the end of a label, since it expects a shortcut there, like "Copy (Ctrl+Shift+C)". A shell name that ends in parentheses loses that part too.
	- Reproduced: 20261004, b23. The Mac menu bar built from a list with "Bash" and "Bash (no rc)" showed "Bash" twice. Test ddg72 failed before the fix.
	- Actual cause:
		- `plain_label` cut a trailing pair of parentheses from every row of the Mac menu bar. It dates from when shortcuts were written into the labels. Shortcuts are now added per row from the key bindings, and the Mac bar is built from rows that never have one, so the cut only ever removed real text.
	- Notes:
		- Before RC1.
	- Actual fix: `plain_label` is gone, and the Mac menu bar shows each label as it is.
	- Swept:
		- `plain_label` had one caller, the Mac menu bar in macmenu.rs.
		- The in-window menus and the right-click menu draw a label whole on every platform.
		- The tab label's short forms read "(no rc)" as a variant on purpose and show it as a star. That isn't a shortcut cut, so it stays.
		- In app.rs, 2 test helpers read a trailing shortcut from sample menus. That's test code only.
	- Verified: unit tests, and clippy for Linux, macOS, and Windows. The native macOS menu code wasn't changed.
	- Branch: shname
	- Commit: 07ad847
	- Test case: ddg72 `a_shell_name_in_the_mac_menu_bar_keeps_its_parentheses`. It failed before the fix and passes after.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: mechanical. The fix only stops a wrong cut, and its test failed before and passes after.
	- Closed: 20261004-091507

- A launch can open on a REPL, because a window that loaded early puts another window's new shell at the top of the list
	- ID: 2026092618142600
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20260926-181426
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: All
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Have a shell installed that the list does not have yet.
		- Start two SilkTerm windows a few seconds apart, and let both scans run.
	- Incorrect behavior: The new shell goes to the top of the list, so the next launch opens on it. Here it was a second Node.js entry, or maybe Python.
	- Expected behavior: A new shell goes at the end, and the default shell stays the same.
	- Reproduced: Yes, on b23 in a unit test of the save. It wasn't seen on screen, since the live list was fixed by hand before this was looked at.
	- Actual cause:
		- A save compared the list against what the window loaded, rather than against the file. There's no file watcher, so a window that loaded before another one saved took out only the entries it knew about. The new entry was left above all of them.
		- The live file fits this. Its second Node.js entry came from a launch with nvm on PATH.
		- shcl isn't at fault. A fresh scan and a reorder both save in the right order through the line-keeping save.
	- Actual fix: The save merges 3 ways against the file. Another window's new entries stay at the end, its removals stay gone, and its edits stay unless this window changed the same entry.
	- Branch: cfgorder
	- Commit: c6d68c1
	- Test case: `a_stale_window_cannot_put_another_windows_find_on_top`, `a_stale_window_keeps_what_another_window_saved`, `a_fresh_file_keeps_the_order_the_scan_found`, `a_fresh_unix_list_arrives_in_the_designed_order`.
	- Verified: 20261004, all 4 pass on dev 76339dd.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the cause was found and pinned by tests, and no repeat has been seen since 20260926.
	- Closed: 20261004-154900

- The pipeline's fuzz soak fails, since a Settings save loses `scroll.inview_tau_ms` at the next launch
	- ID: 2026100311103811
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: High
	- Opened: 20261003-111038
	- Opened by: CC
	- Target OS: All
	- Test environment: b23
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- `SILK_FUZZ_SEED=30 cargo test --bin silkterm fuzz::a_settings_save_moves_no_value_at_the_next_launch`
	- Incorrect behavior: The value loads at launch but isn't found at the next launch after a save. The case is a file with 2 `scroll:` blocks, and the second one has `inview_tau_ms: 219`.
	- Expected behavior: A save doesn't move any value.
	- Reproduced: 20261003 on b23, on dev 3349635 and on f435323, both from before that day's other changes. So none of them caused it.
	- Actual cause:
		- The cause isn't in any of shcl, the renames table, backfill, or the format copy. The rename check tests whether `single_screen_tau_ms` is already in the file, and the file has it only as a comment at column 0 between 2 `scroll:` lines.
		- Since 20261001 (`cfglines`) that check judged the comment where a save that keeps the lines leaves it, which is at column 0 outside `scroll:`, so the rename fired. But shcl keeps the lines or falls back to the whole-file form by what the save changes rather than by the file. The fallback moves the comment into `scroll:`, and then the rename no longer fires. In this file a window size save falls back and a font size save doesn't.
		- So the old name loaded as the new setting before the save, and as itself after it.
	- Origin: 7b3be64 (`cfglines`, 2026100115322367). Confirmed.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261003: Seeds run in order from 0, so every full pipeline run gets to seed 30 in its 20 second soak and stops there. The short soak in a plain test run stops before it. The run from 20261001 got past the soak to the profiler stage, so the change that exposed it is likely between that run and f435323. It wasn't bisected.
		- 20261003: Traced to 7b3be64. Seed 30 passes with the `saved_paths` from before it and fails with its own.
	- Actual fix: The rename check judges a commented line where the whole-file form puts it again. Every save agrees on that place, whichever way it writes. A file with an unreadable line is still judged as it is, since a fallback there is refused.

- shcl 3.0.0-beta1: the conversion checks miss what a beta1 load no longer reports
	- ID: 2026110610154305
	- Type: Task
	- Status: Done
	- Priority: High
	- Opened: 20261106-101543
	- Opened by: CC
	- Parent ID: 2026110609500004
	- Notes:
		- Lines under a heading that doesn't read don't get E018 now. So a current file whose heading isn't UTF-8 kept its layout, though its lines would move to the block above (ddf93).
		- beta1 reads a 2.x `family:[One, Two]` line as the text `[One, Two]`, without a diagnostic, though `migrate` counts it lost. So the conversion counts one line fewer, and later launches no longer name it (`a_file_shcl_cannot_migrate_is_written_new`, `a_setting_the_conversion_cannot_keep_is_reported`).
		- A dogfood file a b10c2009 build stamped Format 3 reads as current. Its comma lists, doubled backslashes, and bare monitor keys don't set anything. No release wrote one.
		- JC 2026-11-06: Must be able to ingest and convert all older shcl formats that have ever been published as [pre-]releases.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261106: ddf93 is fixed on the wip branch. Lines under a heading shcl refused count as unread again, as E018 had them. ddf93 failed before and passes after. The `family:[One, Two]` part and the dogfood files are left.
		- 20261106: A list given to a setting that takes one value doesn't set anything now, and the line counts as one that can't be read. Only a theme's `ansi` takes a list. So the `family:[One, Two]` line is counted when a file is written new, and named at every later launch, as before beta1. Before, it loaded as a font named "[One, Two]". ddf6d and dder4 pass again, and deyry fails without the change.
		- 20261106: `cicd/tests/config-convert/run.bash` expected the b10c2009 spellings for a 2.x backslash path and a theme's ANSI list. It expects beta1's now, single backslashes and the list in brackets.
		- 20261106: The swap and these fixes are on rnd1106.
		- 20261106: A file a b10c2009 dogfood build stamped Format 3 is converted where it stands, when only its comma lists and bare monitor keys fail to read, and every other line reads the same after. Doubled backslashes are halved. A file with any other line beta1 refuses, or a path whose `\n` would become a line break, is left as it is. The launch keeps a copy, named for format 3 (deysd, deyse).
		- 20261106: The releases published so far are shcl v1.0.0-beta1, v1.0.0-beta2, and v1.0.0-rc1 (pre-releases, tags only), v1.0.0, v1.1.0, v1.2.0, and v2.0.0 (also on crates.io), and v3.0.0-beta1. SilkTerm's releases are v1.0.0-beta2 and v1.0.0-beta3, both on shcl 1.2.0. SilkTerm v1.0.0-beta1 was never tagged or released, and wrote `config.toml` rather than shcl.
		- 20261106: Each shcl release before 3.0 wrote one SilkTerm config through its own crate and read it back. They write 4 different files, and all read the same values. After one launch each reads as it did, doesn't lose anything, keeps its copy, and settles (deyst). A v1.0.0-beta2 save and first-launch template convert as beta3's do, the default shell at the top of the list (deysv, deysw).
	- Decisions:
		- 20261106: A list where one value goes is an unread line rather than a value of its own. That's how a beta1 file says it too, and it keeps the conversion's count and the launch's message as they were.
		- 20261106: The fixtures for releases that write the same bytes are one file, named for the range. The release's own crate is what says what each line meant.
		- 20261106: SilkTerm v1.0.0-beta1's `config.toml` doesn't get a fixture, since it was never published and isn't shcl. A Check entry was filed.
	- Branch: rnd1106
	- Test case: ddf93, deyry, ddf6d, dder4, deysd, deyse, deyst (every shcl release before 3.0), deysv and deysw (SilkTerm v1.0.0-beta2), der3m and der3n (v1.0.0-beta3), and `cicd/tests/config-convert/run.bash` (ddf6j). deyst fails with the 2.x respelling skipped.
	- Verified: The backlog quick run passes in all 5 areas, with 1438 unit tests. `cicd/tests/config-convert/run.bash` passes, 113 checks. The test ID check passes.
	- Swept: Every conversion goes through `upgrade`, and the launch converts before the state move reads the monitor sizes. The copy and the converted message for a dogfood file are in `keep_old_format_at` and `publish_keeping`.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: every published format has a fixture that converts with its values. The left-out beta1 TOML has a Check entry.
	- Closed: 20261106-112100
