- Windows: a Git Bash tab keeps its starting folder in the title after a `cd`
	- ID: 2026100709325306
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261007-093253
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: Windows
	- Test environment: vm925w
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Open a Git Bash pane, with the git prompt on.
		- `cd` into another folder.
	- Incorrect behavior: the tab and window title still name the folder the pane started in.
	- Expected behavior: the title follows the shell's folder, as it does for the other shells.
	- Reproduced: once, 20261007 on vm925w at 107b8e6. It wasn't tried with the git prompt off.
		- 20261007 on vm925w with the 46a2193 build, every time. Git prompt on: the title kept the start folder and also showed `[bash]` as a running command. Git prompt off: the window title followed, but only because Git's own prompt sets a title with its path.
	- Possible cause: a bash pane doesn't send a directory report, so the title comes from the process's own folder, which Git Bash may not move on a `cd`. The pane's prompt didn't send a report before the 20261006 prompt change either.
	- Actual cause: It wasn't the report. Git Bash and MSYS2 bash both move their own process folder on a `cd`. Git's `bin\bash.exe` is a launcher, though: it starts `usr\bin\bash.exe` as its child and waits. The pane kept the launcher's process, which never moves, and whose child read as a command that never ends.
	- Actual fix: on Windows a pane started from Git's `bin\bash.exe` or `bin\sh.exe` is read through the real shell, the launcher's child of the same name started within a few seconds of it. Its folder and its commands are what the title and copy-output now see. A launcher is told by its layout, a `usr\bin` copy of the same program one level up.
	- Swept: MSYS2 bash isn't a launcher, and its folder moves (seen on vm925w). Git's `bin\sh.exe` has the same launcher and is handled too. Cygwin bash doesn't have a `usr\bin` copy, so it's left alone. It isn't installed on vm925w, so it wasn't run. WSL isn't a launcher and is unchanged: `wsl.exe` never moves, so its title follows only a shell inside that reports where it is. Linux and macOS bash read `/proc` or `proc_pidinfo`, and the new code is Windows only.
	- Verified: 20261007 on vm925w. The new unit test failed with the fix taken out (the folder stayed at the start folder) and passes with it. The window test failed on the 46a2193 build with the git prompt on and passes on the branch build, prompt off and on. The full Windows unit suite passed. Clippy is clean for Linux and Windows, and the term tests pass on b23.
	- Branch: gbtitle
	- Commit: c24cc57, 70fab8b, dc2842b
	- Test case: `a_git_bash_pane_is_read_past_its_launcher` (ddmjv), `only_the_git_for_windows_layout_is_a_launcher` (ddmjw), window test `cicd/tests/wingui/gbtitle.ps1` (ddmk2), now in the GUI test list.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced, tests failed before and pass after, and the title does what the item expects.
	- Closed: 20261007-114831

- macOS: a double-click on a word after a link selects from the link's start
	- ID: 2026100709325308
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261007-093253
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: All
	- Test environment: b26
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Print `b'https://example.invalid/silk1007 CLIPMARK'`.
		- Double-click "CLIPMARK".
	- Incorrect behavior: the selection runs from the start of the link to the click.
	- Expected behavior: only "CLIPMARK" is selected.
	- Reproduced: 20261007 on b26 at 107b8e6, every time. A double-click on a plain word on another line selected only that word. It wasn't tried on Linux or Windows.
		- 20261007 on b23 at 5939048, by test: the pair rule picks the same span from that line on Linux. The link plays no part. Without the quotes, or with words around the link, only "CLIPMARK" is picked.
	- Actual cause: the line on screen was Python's `b'...'`, and the pair rule read the `'` after the `b` as an opening quote. So the click was inside a quoted pair, and the pair's contents were selected, which start at the link. The same miscount hit any apostrophe: in `don't click 'here'`, a click on "click" took `t click`.
	- Actual fix: a `'` with a letter or digit on both sides is an apostrophe and is neither end of a pair. A quote with a space or punctuation beside it still pairs. The double-click design doc says so.
	- Swept: The other users of quote pairing. Brackets (`distinct_pair`) and a bracket's partner never look at `'`. A triple-click takes the line and doesn't use pairs. Word selection in a tab rename or a dialog box uses `textedit.rs`, which doesn't have pairs. The link hover and a link's span stop before any `'`, since it isn't a link character. A path shape still counts its own apostrophes when it trims a closing `'` (`shapes.rs` `trim_tail`), so `'/srv/O'Brien/docs'` keeps the last quote. That was read rather than run, and is left as rare.
	- Verified: 20261007 on b23. The new test failed before the fix and passes after it. The full unit suite, rustfmt, and clippy passed.
	- Branch: clipquote
	- Commit: 3c6c3ac
	- Test case: `an_apostrophe_is_not_a_quote` (ddmjh).
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced by test, failed before and passes after, and the selection is the one the item expects.
	- Closed: 20261007-112930

- macOS: the interface and terminal fonts are too big
	- ID: 2026100114435561
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Needs external testing: On b26, terminal text at the size `defaults read -g NSFixedPitchFontSize` gives, or about 11 pt when that is unset, and the menus, tabs, and Settings at the size of other apps' interface text. A config with the system size switched off keeps its own size.
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261001-144356
	- Closed: 20261006-140739
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100114435547
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Test environment: b26, Intel Iris Plus 655, macOS 15.8
	- Incorrect behavior: Both the interface fonts and the terminal font are too big. Neither seems to follow the system font size.
	- Expected behavior: Both start from the size macOS uses.
	- Reproduced: No. The Mac was busy, so the cause was found by reading the code and pinned by a test.
	- Actual cause:
		- Sizes macOS reports in points were converted at 96 per inch, as on Windows and Linux. A Mac point already is a logical pixel, so everything came out a third too big. The interface's 13 pt became 17.3.
		- The terminal size was read only from the `NSFixedPitchFontSize` default. Where nobody set it, there was no size to follow and the 17 pixel fallback was used.
	- Actual fix:
		- A Mac point is taken as a logical pixel.
		- The fixed-width size comes from AppKit, which returns its default when nobody has set one. The interface size is AppKit's system size, still 13 pt.
		- The family still comes only from a font somebody picked, so the font list isn't dropped for Menlo.
	- Swept: Both point conversions, the terminal size, and the interface size.
	- Test case: `a_mac_point_is_already_a_logical_pixel` (ddcdy). It fails with the old conversion.
	- Verified: The unit tests on Linux, and clippy for Linux, Windows, and macOS.
	- Branch: macsize
	- Commit: 747356f
	- Closed:

	- Actual cause: The window was already built transparent. The drawing surface wasn't. Metal offers only Opaque and PostMultiplied, never PreMultiplied, and the pick fell back to the first one offered, Opaque. That marks the layer opaque, and the transparency gate saw an opaque surface too.

	- Incorrect behavior: While a tab is being renamed, Paste from the macOS menu bar, which Command+V reaches, pastes into the shell, not the name. The box takes typing, the arrows, Home, End, Backspace, Delete, Ctrl+A and Ctrl+V, and nothing else.

There isn't any file drop or input method handling. The Settings boxes' caret code now uses the same shared rules.

	- ID: 2026100220463754
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done

		- After closing Settings that way, open About and click its link: the link opens.

	- Opened: 20261002-204637
	- Closed: 20261006-141403
	- Opened by: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100220260471
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Test environment: b26
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Open Settings. Hold Ctrl and press Esc, so Settings closes with Ctrl still down. Let go of Ctrl.

- The window size test skips whenever it has to start its own display
	- ID: 2026100512560044
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261005-125600
	- Opened by: CC
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- With the test display not running, run `cicd/tests/startsize/run.bash`.
	- Incorrect behavior: It starts the display and xfwm4, then says "no window manager on :98" and exits 3. The pipeline prints a warning and goes on, so the test only runs when its display is already up.
	- Expected behavior: It waits for the window manager it started, then runs.
	- Reproduced: 20261005 on b23, twice in a row. With the display started first and 2 seconds of wait, the same run passed.
	- Possible cause: `gui-headless.bash start --wm` returns before xfwm4 sets `_NET_SUPPORTING_WM_CHECK`, and the test reads it at once.
	- Note: Found while working 2026100314050016.
	- Actual cause:
		- `gui-headless.bash start --wm` returned as soon as xfwm4 was forked, so the test asked for the window manager before it was up.
		- Waiting for it showed 2 more faults. xfwm4 joined the desktop's own session through `SESSION_MANAGER`, so each one stopped here was restarted by the desktop onto the test display, where it took the next run's screen. And the pid kept for `stop` was a subshell's, so `stop` left xfwm4 and any launched app running.
	- Actual fix:
		- `start --wm` waits until the window manager responds, up to 10 seconds (`CICD_HEADLESS_WM_WAIT`). If it doesn't, it stops the window manager, and the display too when this call started it, and fails with a message.
		- Programs on the test display leave the desktop's session. That includes the demo recorder too.
		- Background launches record the program's own pid, and `stop` waits for each one to exit.
	- Swept: `grep -rn gui-headless` over the repo. `start --wm` callers: the window size test and the scroll test. Only the window size test reads the window manager itself. The scroll test, the delete-config test, the wallpaper resize test, config-convert, and the profiler stage use `start`, and none of them reads the window manager. The demo recorder starts its own xfwm4 with a fixed wait, and got the session fix only.
	- Verified: from a cold display, the window size test skipped 2 of 2 on the old code and passed 3 of 3 after. There were 40 stop and start cycles without a failure, where 3 in 30 had failed before the session fix. A window manager that hangs or exits makes `start --wm` fail and doesn't leave a display behind. The scroll test's tmux scene, the demo test, and the install test pass.

- A passing unit test run keeps its test folder
	- ID: 2026100418554244
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261004-185542
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100220260484, 2026100314050010
	- Target OS: All
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Run the whole unit test suite with every test passing.
	- Incorrect behavior: The run ends with "test files kept in" and leaves its `test_silkterm_<stamp>` folder behind.
	- Expected behavior: A run without a failed test removes its own folder.
	- Reproduced: 20261004, twice on b23, each with all 1117 tests passing.
	- Possible cause: any panic marks the run as failed, and `a_poisoned_lock_is_taken_as_it_stands` (ddgkc) panics on purpose inside `catch_unwind`. Run alone it doesn't make a folder, so the keep doesn't show then.
	- Origin: Item 2026100314050010 added ddgkc after 2026100220260484 made any panic keep the folder. Confirmed: a full passing run kept its folder, and ddgkc was the only panic in it.
	- Cause: the panic hook runs before anything catches the panic, so it can't tell a caught panic from a failed test.
	- Fixed: a test that panics on purpose catches it through `testdir::catch_expected_panic`, and the hook leaves the folder alone for a panic raised inside it. ddgkc uses it. Any other panic still keeps the folder.
	- Swept: `catch_unwind`, `should_panic`, and `set_hook` across `source/`. ddgkc was the only deliberate panic. `fuzz.rs` catches only to name the seed and then fails the test, so it keeps the folder as it should. `ctl.rs` chains a hook in the app, not in tests. There's one test binary, and there aren't any integration tests. A full run with output shown printed one panic before the fix and only the 2 deliberate ones after.
	- Note: a test that fails before any test has asked for the folder isn't counted, since the hook is put in by the first ask. It's left as it was.
	- Test case: `a_panic_a_test_expects_does_not_keep_the_folder` (ddgzm), and `no_test_catches_a_panic_behind_the_run_folders_back` (ddgzn), which fails on a bare `catch_unwind` or `should_panic` outside `testdir.rs` and `fuzz.rs`. `cicd/tests/testdir/run.bash` step A2 now runs ddgzm too. Both failed with the hook check and the ddgkc change taken out, and that run kept its folder. Both pass with them in.
	- Verified: a full `cargo test` passed, 1128 tests, and left nothing in its temp dir. The same run before the fix kept its folder. `cicd/tests/testdir/run.bash` passed. Clippy, fmt, and the test ID check are clean.
	- Branch: testkeep
	- Commit: 4618fab
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: intent clear, reproduced, tests fail before the fix and pass after.
	- Closed: 20261004-221448

	- ID: 2026100410244885

	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261004-102448
	- Opened by: CC
	- Target OS: All
	- Test environment: b26
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Run `cargo test` on a box whose config a newer build would refresh, such as an old commented default.
	- Incorrect behavior: The test process loads the live config and writes it back after migrating it. On b26 a commented `idle_release` default line changed from false to true.
	- Expected behavior: A test run leaves the real config file alone.
	- Reproduced: 20261004 on b26. The system log shows the test binary starting the same second the file was written.
	- Notes:
		- Note: 20261004, the change on b26 didn't alter behavior, since the set value below it was untouched. The next dogfood launch would make the same edit.
		- Note: 20261004, the private pipeline's test runs on b26 do this too. There are 2 ways out: test runs default to a throwaway home, or loading never writes under test. The tests that read the live config on purpose (G6) need checking either way.
	- Actual cause: The first settings read in a test process runs the launch steps, and those write the file back when a newer build would change it. Nothing told a test run apart.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261004: A test process never writes the box's own config or anything in its folder, the data folder included. Reading it stays as it was, so the tests that read it on purpose (G6) still do. A write to a file a test picked for itself still goes through.
		- A throwaway home for test runs wasn't taken. It would also stop the reads that G6 relies on.
	- Actual fix: Under test, every write of the settings file first asks whether the file is in the box's own settings or data folder, and skips it if so. That includes the launch steps, saves, the rating, the reset, and every backup beside the file. The wallpaper history, the bash prompt script, and the shell integration record ask the same. A normal build is unchanged.
	- Swept: every writer in config.rs (the shared atomic write, which handles the launch refreshes, conversions, the non-UTF-8 rewrite, `config_backup_*` and `config.format<N>.shcl` copies, saves, the rating, the shell adoption, the default shell move, window size and monitor saves, and key reverts), the `.bak` copy and move, the folder made for a missing file, the move of an old config from `~/.config` on Windows and macOS, `.wallpaper-history`, the bash prompt script, and `shell-integration.installed`. Other writers in the tree touch only test folders or files outside the settings folder.
	- Verified: the new test fails with the check turned off, in each of its 4 cases, and passes with it on. The full unit suite and clippy pass on b23. The live config on b23 was byte-identical before and after the runs. It wasn't run on Windows or macOS.
	- Branch: testcfg
	- Commit: c98e3c9
	- Test case: `a_test_run_never_writes_the_boxs_own_config` (ddgbt). A file in a folder of its own stands in for the box's, without an override set. A launch, a save, a rating, a key revert, and a reset must leave the folder as it was, for a stale commented default, a 2.x file, a file that isn't UTF-8, and a missing file.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced through a stand-in file, and the test fails without the fix and passes with it. Only test runs change.
	- Closed: 20261004-113953

- With Free resources when idle on, a window on screen but not focused is let go, goes black, and stays black until typed into
	- ID: 2026100319134501
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261003-191345
	- Opened by: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100312470535, 2026100312470540
	- Target OS: Windows
	- Test environment: vm925w
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Turn on Free resources when idle with a short idle time, and Transparency.
		- Minimize the window, then restore it without giving it focus.
		- Wait past the idle time with the window in view.
	- Incorrect behavior: The window is let go while still on screen, with "(resource conservation mode)" in its title. It keeps its last picture for a while, then goes black, and stays black until typed into.
	- Expected behavior: A window in view keeps painting, or paints again on its own.
	- Reproduced: Yes, on vm925w in the builds from before and after the 2026100312470535 fix, with another program loading the GPU. It wasn't tried without the load, so it isn't known if the load matters. It was only tried with Transparency on, which draws through DX12.
		- 20261004: It was also seen without any load. The window went black within 4 seconds of being let go in view. With Transparency off it kept its last picture.
	- Actual cause:
		- With Transparency on, Windows draws the window through a composition visual, and the window doesn't have a surface of its own. Letting the device go takes the picture with it.
		- An unfocused window in view is let go after "Minutes otherwise", which on this path doesn't leave anything on screen. The load only put off when it went black.
	- Actual fix: A window without a surface of its own is never let go while in view. It waits until it is minimized, and then for "Minutes when hidden". Every other window is unchanged.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261004: Verified on vm925w, without load and under a lighter load than the one that hung the box: with Transparency on, a window left unfocused in view kept its picture past the idle time, and still let go and came back when minimized. With Transparency off nothing changed. The build from dev went black in the same steps.
		- 20261004: Verified: both new unit tests fail with the fixes taken out and pass with them. The full unit suite, clippy for Linux and Windows, and fmt pass.
	- Swept: `release_deadline` is the one decision, and both of its callers, the release and the wake set for it, go through `State::release_deadline`. Dialogs are never let go on idle.
	- Note: 20261004, the "Minutes otherwise" help still says an unfocused window waits that long. On Windows with Transparency on, a window in view now keeps its device. So the help needed rewording.
		- Decision: 20261004, reworded. The help and the config comment now say a window on screen with Transparency on is never let go on Windows.
	- Branch: idlewake
	- Commit: 7687c4e
	- Test case: `a_window_that_would_go_blank_is_never_let_go_in_view` (ddga8). Also the `idlewake` Windows GUI scenario (ddgaa), not in the pipeline.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced without load, fixed, and the test fails on the old code. The change follows the design goal that a window on screen never gives anything up.
	- Closed: 20261004-112231

- After waking from Free resources when idle, the window sometimes shows only the prompt's last character until typed into
	- ID: 2026100319134502
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261003-191345
	- Opened by: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100312470535, 2026100312470540
	- Target OS: Windows
	- Test environment: vm925w
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Turn on Free resources when idle with a short idle time.
		- Let the window go idle while minimized, then restore it.
	- Incorrect behavior: The earlier text is missing, and only the last `>` of the prompt shows. Typing brings the rest back.
	- Expected behavior: The window shows everything it showed before it went idle.
	- Reproduced: Yes, now and then, on vm925w in the builds from before and after the 2026100312470535 fix, with another program loading the GPU. It wasn't tried without the load.
		- 20261004: Seen again on vm925w under a lighter load, with Transparency on: the device was rebuilt while the window didn't have a size, and the shell's screen went to 2 by 1 and back. It wasn't seen in 6 restores without load. The load only makes the gap easier to hit.
		- 20261004: Earlier runs show it with Transparency off too.
	- Actual cause:
		- On Windows a restore stops reporting minimized a moment before the window gets its size back. A rebuild in that gap read a 0x0 window, took 1x1 as its size, and shrank the grid to 2 columns and 1 row.
		- The console host reflowed its screen at that width. When the real size came back it repainted only the prompt's last character, and the earlier text stayed in the scrollback.
	- Actual fix: A window whose last resize was to nothing counts as hidden until a real size arrives, so nothing is drawn or rebuilt in the gap. Coming back into view now brings the device back by itself, since the desktop's repaint that used to do it can arrive inside the gap.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261004: Verified on vm925w, with and without the lighter load, Transparency on and off: after each restore with or without focus, the window showed what it showed before it was let go, and every rebuild came back at the full window size.
		- 20261004: The first try at the fix left a window let go while minimized blank after a restore without focus, because the repaint came inside the gap and nothing else woke it. It was fixed by the wake on coming back into view.
		- 20261004: Verified: the new unit test fails with the fix taken out and passes with it.
	- Swept: `hidden()` is the one hidden test, read by both render entry points and the rebuild. Every reader of the window's size: the dialogs, which are never minimized on their own, and the surface setup, which gets to a rebuild only through `rebuild_gpu`. `heal_gpu` runs only on a Linux console return, where a minimized window keeps its size.
	- Branch: idlewake
	- Commit: 7687c4e
	- Test case: `a_window_with_no_area_is_hidden_whatever_the_minimized_answer` (ddga9). Also the restore checks in the `idlewake` Windows GUI scenario (ddgaa), not in the pipeline, which catch the gap only now and then.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the cause was caught on the box, and no rebuild at the wrong size was seen after the fix, with or without load.
	- Closed: 20261004-112231

- macOS: a tab never names the program running in it
	- ID: 2026100410053273
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Needs external testing: A look in a real SilkTerm window on b26: a tab running an editor, and one running a `sudo` command, names the program.
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261004-100532
	- Opened by: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100408214204
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Test environment: b26
	- Incorrect behavior: The tab label never shows the program running in the shell, such as an editor.
	- Expected behavior: The same as on Linux.
	- Reproduced: 20261004 on b26, through the lookup a tab uses. It didn't give a name for a running `sleep`.
	- Possible cause: The running program's name is read from `/proc` (`proc_comm` in term.rs), which macOS doesn't have. The shell's folder had the same fault, fixed under 2026100408214204.
	- Actual cause:
		- The name came only from `/proc`, so on macOS every lookup came back empty. The same lookup decides the minimap's per-program switch, which never saw a program there either.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261013: The test failed on b26 once GNU coreutils was on PATH: there `sleep` is a link to `gsleep`, and a Mac names the file a link points to, so the code was right and the test wasn't. It now starts `/bin/sleep` by full path. Verified: it fails before and passes after on b26, and passes on Linux. Swept: the 6 other tests that start `sleep` never check its name, and nothing else reads a spawned program's name. It's on branch macfix.
	- Actual fix:
		- On macOS the name comes from the process's short BSD info, the first 16 bytes of its name, about the same as Linux's 15. That works for another user's process too. `proc_name` was tried first and doesn't give anything for a root process, so a `sudo` command would have stayed unnamed. Linux is unchanged.
	- Swept: every `/proc` read in the source, and everything that names a pane's foreground program. The tab label and the minimap both go through `proc_comm`. Copy-output and the reported-folder check use the foreground process group only, which macOS reports. The config busy check, wallpaper memory test, and profiler CPU name are Linux only on purpose.
	- Verified: on b26 the new test fails with the old lookup (no name) and with `proc_name` (no name for pid 1), and passes with the fix. All 24 terminal tests pass there. The terminal tests on Linux, rustfmt, and clippy for Linux and macOS x86_64 pass.
	- Branch: maccomm
	- Commit: 0db9f44
	- Test case: `the_foreground_program_is_named_by_its_process_group` (ddg92). A program leading its own process group is named by the group id, and pid 1, root's, is named too.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: reproduced on b26, and the test failed there before the fix and passes after. A real window still needs a look.
	- Closed: 20261004-102407

- A current-format config that isn't UTF-8 loads as defaults with no message, and a Settings save on it says it worked but writes nothing
	- ID: 2026100315581313
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Needs external testing: The new unit tests on Windows, at the next vm925w run.
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261003-155813
	- Opened by: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100312470546, 2026100316135866
	- Target OS: All
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Put a byte that isn't valid UTF-8 into a config file that already has the current Format line.
		- Launch, then change a setting in Settings and save.
	- Incorrect behavior: The launch shows defaults and says nothing about the file. The save reports success, and the file is unchanged.
	- Expected behavior: The launch says the file couldn't be read. A save either writes or says it didn't.
	- Reproduced: 20261003 on b23, on dev 7895ffa. A unit test loaded the file as all defaults, and `persist` reported that it saved but didn't write anything. It was first found by reading the code while working 2026100312470546, which handles only an old-format file.
	- Origin: The not-UTF-8 read in `read_settings_text` returned nothing for a current file, and `persist` took nothing to read as nothing to do. Item 2026100312470546 kept that on purpose for a current file. Confirmed.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261003: First fix (badutf8, 54c8d73): the launch read every line that decodes, named the others, and every save refused, leaving the file as it was. Replaced by the second fix below, per the Decisions row.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261003: Rewrite the file and keep a backup, rather than refusing saves. Start over with defaults in the worst case.
		- 20261003: The rewrite happens at launch, rather than at the first save. The launch already does every other format rewrite and says it once with the window up. A first save is often a resize or the rating, which nobody connects with the file.
	- Against: Item 2026100312470546 left a current file that isn't UTF-8 alone. This item's first decision replaces that.
	- Actual fix:
		- At launch, such a file is copied to `config_backup_<time>_format-v3.shcl` the way an old-format file is, then written again without the lines that don't decode. It keeps its own layout as long as every other line reads the same without them.
		- A block heading that doesn't decode would move its lines into the block above. That file, and one where nothing is left that sets anything, is written new from the template with every setting that still reads. When there's nothing to keep, that's the defaults.
		- A line of the SHCL footer that doesn't decode is put back as it came, since an editor saving in Latin-1 always garbles its copyright sign.
		- The terminal names the lines and the copy. A "Settings file rewritten" notice says the same once the window is up. The "Settings not saved" refusal for this case is gone.
		- A launch that finds the file busy leaves it, and the next save or rating write does the same rewrite and says it the same way.
		- `upgrade` in config.rs makes the choice for this case too, and the copy is made by the same writer.
	- Swept: Every writer of the file. `persist` (Settings save, window size, font zoom, per-monitor sizes, copy toggles, shells found at launch) reads through `read_doc`, which now gets the rewritten text. The rating write reads it too and writes through the same writer. `adopt_default_shell` uses `read_doc`. The launch's other steps read with `read_to_string`, so they run on the rewritten file, or don't write anything to a busy one. The window size refresh reads the rewritten text. `--reset-config` moves the bytes aside unread. The writer keeps a copy before replacing any settings file that isn't UTF-8, whoever calls it.
	- Test case: `a_current_file_that_is_not_utf8_drops_only_those_lines` (ddf93), `a_launch_writes_a_current_file_that_is_not_utf8_again` (ddf94), and `a_save_on_a_current_file_that_is_not_utf8_writes_it_again` (ddf95) fail with the old behavior put back in `upgrade` and pass now. `a_footer_line_that_is_not_utf8_goes_back_to_the_original` (ddf96), seen to fail with the footer step off. `a_notice_for_dropped_lines_names_them_and_the_copy` (ddf92). Fuzz target `a_rewrite_for_lines_that_are_not_utf8_settles` (ddf97). `cicd/tests/config-convert/run.bash` (ddf6j) checks the rewrite, the copy, the terminal line, and the new notice. Those checks failed on a build with the old behavior put back.
		- Commented out, since they pin the refusal: `a_current_file_shcl_cannot_read_is_left_alone` (ddf6f), `a_current_file_that_is_not_utf8_loads_what_reads` (ddf75), `a_save_on_a_current_file_that_is_not_utf8_is_refused` (ddf76), `a_notice_for_lines_that_are_not_utf8_says_so` (ddf77), and the pipeline test's left-alone and `notsaved` checks.
	- Verified: The unit suite passes, 1083 tests, and a 60 s soak of both upgrade fuzz targets. fmt is clean, clippy is clean for Linux and Windows, and the test ID, markdown spacing, and table checks pass. The pipeline test passes, notice window included. A whole config saved in Latin-1 was written again in one launch with its footer whole, and a second launch changed nothing.
	- Branch: badutf8b
	- Commit: 3f23f69
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: does what the decision says, its tests failed before the fix and pass after, and the sweep is answered.
	- Closed: 20261003-172228

- Settings: the revert arrow on "Program's own title" does nothing
	- ID: 2026100314050001
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done

	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261003-140500
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: All
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Open Settings, Tabs. Turn "Program's own title" away from its default.
		- Click its revert arrow.
	- Incorrect behavior: The box doesn't change back. `revert` lists every toggle in one outer match, and `TabShowsTitle` is missing from it. The key falls to the slider arm at the end, which does nothing for a toggle.
	- Expected behavior: The box goes back to its default, like every other toggle.

	- Origin: d83fb601 (2026-09-20) added the inner arm for this key but not the outer one. No earlier review saw it. Confirmed.
	- Possible cause: There are 14 per-key accessors in `settings_ui.rs` that end in a catch-all `_` arm, so a key left out of one compiles and quietly does the wrong thing. `ui_spec.rs` says `Key` exists so that a missed key fails to compile.
	- Actual cause: as above.
	- Actual fix: every accessor now names every key, its own kind one by one and the rest through one list per kind of row (`keys_of!`). A key left out of an accessor, or new in `ui_spec.rs`, no longer compiles. Slider and switch values are read through one function each, for the shown value, the default, and the revert, so those lists exist once. `env_flag` takes a switch from a list, and each switch keeps its own cached value.
	- Sweep: the `_` arms in `get_f32`, `set_f32`, `get_toggle`, `set_toggle`, `get_radio`, `set_radio`, `get_col`, `set_col`, `default_col`, `is_default`, `default_f32`, `revert`, `get_text`, and `set_text`. There's the same kind of arm in `pick.rs` (5 on `Field`), in `pane.rs` on `term::Task`, and in `app.rs` `env_flag`.
	- Note: `env_flag`'s arm already ties 2 debug switches together. `SILK_IDLEDBG` falls into `SILK_DLGDBG`'s cached value, so whichever is read first decides both.
	- Swept: all 14 accessors named above. The 5 `Field` arms in `pick.rs` and the `term::Task` arm in `pane.rs` name their variants. `env_flag` gives `SILK_IDLEDBG` its own value. Left on purpose: `assoc_of` and `disabled_tip` in `settings_ui.rs`, which return a value for a few keys and nothing for the rest. The other `_` arms there match on row kinds or numbers rather than keys. The other cached switches, in `perf.rs` and `pane.rs`, have one switch each.
	- Test case: `every_revert_arrow_puts_its_row_back_to_the_default` (ddf52) failed before the fix and passes after. `every_row_kind_matches_its_key_list` (ddf57) checks the key lists against the rows. `each_debug_switch_reads_its_own_variable` (ddf59) failed on `SILK_IDLEDBG` before the fix and passes after.
	- Branch: keyarms

- Settings: a revert arrow leaves the value in force when a save put it above its commented default
	- ID: 2026100309455678
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20261003-094556
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100307252506, 2026100219054510
	- Target OS: All
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Start from a fresh config. In Settings, untick Choose automatically on the Silk tab and Apply. Click its revert arrow and press OK. Relaunch.
	- Incorrect behavior: Choose automatically is still off. The same goes for any hotkey set on the Keys tab.
	- Expected behavior: it is back on, and the file is as it was installed.
	- Reproduced: 20261003 on b23, by test, for `performance.automatic` and `keys.close_pane`. `scroll.smooth` went back, but left a second copy of its commented line.
	- Actual cause: a save adds a set value as a new line, sometimes above the template's commented line. The revert took the last line for the path, which was the comment, and left the value alone.
	- Actual fix: the revert edits the setting's active line. Where the template's commented line is already in the file, the value line goes, rather than becoming a second copy of it.
	- Test case: `a_revert_takes_out_a_value_saved_beside_its_default` (ddev5). It failed before the fix and passes after.
	- Swept: the cleared font family box goes through the same line lookup, and comments out the active line too.
	- Branch: keystab
	- Commit: 9f26b24
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: hard to check by hand, and its test failed before the fix and passes on dev.
	- Closed: 20261003-124705

- A pipeline run dies at the Windows GUI stage when a box is held elsewhere
	- ID: 2026092618254900
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20260926-182549
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Hold vm925w's host lock from another process.
		- Run `cicd/cicd.bash -y --no-publish`.
	- Incorrect behavior: The harness queues for the lock, prints "still queued", and the run stops with "a windows gui scenario failed". No dogfood build is made.
	- Expected behavior: A locked or unreachable box is reported and stepped over, as the stage's own comment says. Only a scenario that ran and failed stops the run.
	- Reproduced: Yes, on b23 on 20260926 at 18:25, with vm925w held by a nemo-anywhere run.
	- Possible cause: The lock's "still queued" exit is passed to `cicd.bash` as the harness's failure.
	- Actual cause:
		- `--optional` applied to a box that was off, rather than one held elsewhere. The lock's wait ran out and its exit was taken for the harness's.
		- Both boxes were asked for at once, so the free one was lost with the held one.
	- Estimated effort: Low
	- Actual effort: Low
	- Actual fix: With `--optional`, each box is held and run on in turn. A box whose wait runs out before the command starts is reported and skipped. The command's own exit is still passed on.
	- Branch: winlock
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/win-remote/run.bash`, against a stand-in lock. It was seen to fail on the old runner.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: pipeline only, and its test failed before the fix.
	- Closed: 20260930-073126

- Four unit tests fail on Windows
	- ID: 2026093010080316
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Priority|Severity: Avg
	- Opened: 20260930-100803
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: Windows
	- Test environment: vm925w, `cargo test`
	- Steps to reproduce: Run `cargo test` on Windows.
	- Incorrect behavior:
		- `the_wallpaper_box_follows_the_rotate_switch` and `the_default_wallpaper_folder_is_found_in_the_usual_place` compare `C:/pics` against `/pics`.
		- `a_second_apply_diffs_against_the_first` looks for a Unix line ending in `app.rs`, and a Windows checkout has CRLF.
		- `arming_a_copy_waits_for_the_term_instead_of_giving_up` failed with "a try can lose the race".
	- Expected behavior: They pass, as on Linux.
	- Reproduced: 20260930 on vm925w. The tests date from 09-26, and Windows was only cross-built since 09-19, so they had never run there.
	- Possible cause: The first 3 are faults in the tests rather than the product. The last may be timing on a slower box.
	- Actual cause: All 4 are faults in the tests. None of them is timing.
		- `/pics` and `/elsewhere` have a root but no drive, so Windows doesn't count them as absolute. The folder resolves against the config dir's drive, which gives `C:/pics`. That is the right answer on Windows.
		- The `app.rs` and `pane.rs` checks cut a function body at an LF-only `}` line. On a CRLF checkout nothing matched. The `app.rs` one didn't find an end. The `pane.rs` one ran on to the end of the file, into code that does call `try_lock`, which is where "a try can lose the race" came from.
	- Progress log:
		- 20260930: All 4 were seen failing on vm925w at d9adce8, and passing there on the branch.
	- Actual fix: The 2 wallpaper tests use a folder that is absolute on the platform they run on, `C:/pics` or `C:/elsewhere` on Windows. They still check that a named folder is used as given and outranks the image. The 2 source checks turn CRLF into LF before cutting, as the shell-integration doc check already did. `.gitattributes` is unchanged.
	- Branch: wintests
	- Commit: 731d528
	- Test case: The 4 tests named above. They were seen to fail on vm925w before the fix and pass after.
	- Verified: The 4 tests on vm925w, before and after, and the same 4 on Linux. Clippy passed with warnings as errors, native and for the Windows target.
	- Swept:
		- Source files read by tests: every `include_str!` of a `.rs` file. The other 5 split at `"\nmod tests {"`, read by `.lines()`, or already cut at `"\n}"`, so a CRLF checkout doesn't change them. The build-inputs test only matches include names.
		- Rooted paths: every `PathBuf::from("/` and `Path::new("/` in the tests. The rest go into pure functions or are compared as given, never through an absolute check.
		- Sleeps in tests: the tip dwell, the uptime check, the lock-for-frame test, the busy-file polls, and the shell-exit waits. Each sleeps at least as long as it checks, or polls with a cap.
		- The Windows run this item came from named only these 4. That full suite wasn't run again.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: test fixes only, and all 4 failed before the fix and pass after on Windows.
	- Closed: 20260930-125357

- Implement leak and static checks of the Rust code run as part of CI/CD
	- ID: 2026101714015789
	- Type: Task
	- Status: Done
	- Priority: Avg
	- Opened: 20261017-140157
	- Opened by: JC
	- Requirements:
		- For all:
			- The checks cover first-party and third-party code. Vendored code is included.
				- Third-party code gets every leak, memory, and correctness check named here, and what they find gets fixed. Only our code gets linted.
				- CodeQL reports only on source inside the database's root. For its run, vendor the dependencies into the tree first (`cargo vendor`).
			- Any report fails the test that made it.
			- Any leak is fixed, in our code or third-party code. If the fix has to wait, it gets a backlog item, and the test that shows it turns the check off with that item's ID beside it.
			- A `--leakcheck` flag adds the slow checks:
				- CodeQL, from a pinned CLI run locally. No hosted service.
				- A soak test. It loops through the program's main actions headless, and fails if the heap at round 2N is larger than at round N by more than a set margin. The heap report is kept as a pipeline artifact.
			- Every tool is pinned and runs in the build container or lint image, never installed on the host.
			- Each new gate is watched to fail before it's trusted, by planting the leak it's meant to catch and seeing it go red.
			- Known-advisory scans run on every full run: `cargo deny check advisories` or `cargo audit`. They cover third-party code only, which is the point.
		- For Rust:
			- Safe Rust leaks only through `Rc` or `Arc` cycles, `mem::forget`, `Box::leak`, and collections that grow forever. Real leaks and memory errors come from `unsafe` and FFI, in our crates or in dependencies.
			- Every full run builds the whole test suite with AddressSanitizer and LeakSanitizer, in a build dir of its own.
				- `RUSTFLAGS=-Zsanitizer=address cargo +NIGHTLY test -Zbuild-std --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`.
				- That needs a dated nightly, pinned beside the stable toolchain. Sanitizers aren't stable.
				- Every crate built from source is instrumented, dependencies included.
			- If the code starts threads, every full run also builds the tests with ThreadSanitizer (`-Zsanitizer=thread`), in another build dir.
			- Every full run runs the test suite under Miri: `cargo +NIGHTLY miri test`. It catches undefined behavior in `unsafe` code, ours and dependencies', and fails on memory still allocated at exit.
				- It moves behind `--leakcheck` only if a full run measures too slow.
			- A heap-growth test with `dhat` in testing mode reads `dhat::HeapStats` at round N and 2N in-process. It's the soak test for a library with no main program.
			- clippy runs with `-D warnings`, plus `clippy::mem_forget` and `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks`.
			- Every `unsafe` block has a `// SAFETY:` comment.
			- Traps:
				- Without `-Zbuild-std`, std isn't instrumented. ASan mostly copes, but TSan gives false reports.
				- Without an explicit `--target`, the sanitizer flags reach build scripts and proc macros, and the build fails in odd places.
				- LSan reports at process exit, so a leak fails the whole test binary, not one test. Rerun with `--test-threads=1` and a test-name filter to find which.
				- Miri can't call FFI and has limited file and network access. A test that needs them gets `#[cfg_attr(miri, ignore)]` with a one-line reason. It's not silently left out.
				- Miri doesn't count memory reachable from a `static` as a leak, so a cache in a static that grows forever passes. The soak test catches that.
				- heaptrack and dhat both see only the global allocator. A crate that maps memory itself, or a custom allocator, hides it.
				- ASan and TSan can't share a build, and heaptrack can't share one with either. The soak test uses a plain build.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261017: JC: CI/CD leak tests, and all tests, include third-party and vendored code, but only code that gets run by end users. Anything wrong goes on the backlog for a fix.
			- Read as: crates built into a release binary for a release target. Build scripts, proc macros, dev-dependencies, and test-only tools are left out.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261017: Priority Avg is a best guess, since none was given. It was split into 5 child items, worked one at a time, the cheap static checks first. This item closes when they do.
		- 20261104: All 8 children are Done, the CodeQL one last. clippy denies mem_forget and undocumented_unsafe_blocks through -D warnings.
	- Test case: its 8 children's tests, the last being the CodeQL planted and clean runs on 2026110315304782
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: every child closed with its own test.
	- Closed: 20261104-181800

- Leak checks: the soak driver and its heap check
	- ID: 2026110117065477
	- Type: Task
	- Status: Done
	- Priority: Avg
	- Opened: 20261101-170654
	- Opened by: CC
	- Parent ID: 2026101913370214
	- Requirements:
		- A test script loops the main actions headless on a private display: a tab, a split, typing into a real PTY, the Settings dialog, and a second window, each opened and closed.
		- Every shell is a harmless test script, given by `--shell` and the test config's shell list, never the user's shell or its config.
		- The heap at round N and 2N comes from heaptrack on a plain build, pinned in the build image, and the test fails when 2N is over N by more than a set margin. The heaptrack data and a summary are kept for the step to save.
		- It's watched to fail on a planted leak.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261101: `cicd/tests/soak/run.bash` runs the debug build under heaptrack on a private Xvfb with xfwm4, in the build image. Each round opens a tab and a split and types into both, closes the split, opens and closes the Settings dialog, opens a window, types into it and closes it, then closes the tab. It runs 6 rounds and then 6 more, in about 2.5 minutes.
		- 20261101: Each shell notes its pid with what it got, so the test fails when a hotkey did nothing and the typing went to an older pane, or a closed pane's shell lives on.
		- 20261101: The heap after each round is the lowest live heap in a quiet 2 s after it. On llvmpipe it moves between 2 levels about 120 KiB apart, and round 6 to 12 grew 4 KiB, -68 and -30 in 3 runs. The margin is 256 KiB.
		- 20261101: `--plant` preloads a shim that leaks 64 KiB in the program each time it starts a child, 3 a round. Round 6 to 12 then grew 1152 KiB, and the test failed.
		- 20261101: `--out` keeps heaptrack's data and the per-round summary, about 7 MB for 2 rounds. The step that saves them is 2026110117065496.
		- 20261101: It didn't find anything, and the heap reads flat.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261101: The heap at a round comes from heaptrack's raw data, read by `heapat.py`, since `heaptrack_print` gives only the peak and what was left at exit.
		- 20261101: It uses the debug build, which is the plain one stage 2 makes before the leak checks. The release build comes later, in stage 5.
		- 20261101: The planted leak hooks the spawn, since the PTY is opened by raw syscalls, so the program itself stays untouched.
		- 20261101: heaptrack is trixie's 1.5.0+dfsg1-5, pinned by version in a layer of its own after CodeQL, so adding it didn't rebuild the toolchains.
		- 20261101: A new window is a process of its own, so only the spawn side is measured. The window's own process isn't.
	- Verified: 20261101. The test passed at round 6 to 12 once in the rebuilt build image, and twice in a stand-in image, the old one plus the same heaptrack layer. It failed with `--plant`, and with the new tab key swapped for one that does nothing. `--out` kept both files. `cicd/cicd.bash --backlog-run-quick` with all 5 areas, the header test ddghe included, `test-id.py --check` and its test, ruff, mypy, and shellcheck pass.
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/soak/run.bash` (der46), not in the pipeline until 2026110117065496.
	- Branch: rnd1101b
	- Closed: 20261101-174350

- Make sure shcl files from v1.0.0-beta3 are accurately converted to the latest shcl spec
	- ID: 2026102818080401
	- Type: Enhancement
	- Status: Done
	- Opened: 20261028-180804
	- Opened by: JC
	- Requirements:
		- Files from v1.0.0-beta3 are accurately converted to the latest shcl spec.
		- The latest spec is listed as v2 but is actually working toward v3 beta.
	- Notes:
		- Pre-next-cut.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261101: beta3 wrote one shcl file, the config, with its themes and shell list in it, through shcl 1.2. The wallpaper history it also writes is a plain list.
		- 20261101: Test files were made the way beta3 wrote them, from its template on a first launch, and from a Settings save that changed every setting, added a theme, and set the shell list.
		- 20261101: Every value came through, renames and the blink rate included. The theme's ANSI lists, the shell list, and its dates read the same.
		- 20261101: There was a gap, since beta3 didn't have performance profiles. A file with its own scroll timings, halo, outline, blur, or wallpaper switch came up under the automatic profile, which drew the profile's values in place of the user's. Of the beta3 save's values, 16 read that way.
		- 20261101: It's fixed in the conversion. A file from before the profiles, with a governed row set to anything but Max silk's value, comes up on Custom with "Choose automatically" off. An untouched beta3 file stays automatic.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261101: "From before the profiles" means a file in an older format without any `performance` line at all, active or commented. Every template since the profiles has those lines, so a later file keeps the profile it says.
		- 20261101: A governed row equal to Max silk's value doesn't count as a look of its own. beta3's template had the scroll timings active at those values, so an untouched file would otherwise lose the hardware test.
		- 20261101: It's done in `upgrade`, so it happens once, keeps the same backup, and also handles a file a busy launch left for the next save.
	- Test case: `a_file_beta3_saved_keeps_every_setting` (der3m), `a_file_beta3_wrote_on_first_launch_stays_automatic` (der3n), `only_a_look_set_before_the_profiles_comes_up_custom` (der3p), and the beta3 case in `cicd/tests/config-convert/run.bash` (ddf6j). der3m and der3p fail with the profile step off and pass with it.
	- Verified: The backlog quick run passes, with all 5 areas and 1417 unit tests. Windows clippy is clean. `cicd/tests/config-convert/run.bash` passes, 113 checks, the beta3 case included.
	- Swept: Every path that converts an older file goes through `upgrade`: the launch, the in-memory read for a busy file, the launch steps the rating check replays, and the writer every save goes through. Both its old-format arms, in place and written new, take the step.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the tests failed before the fix and pass after. The profile choice has a Check entry.
	- Closed: 20261101-170218

		- 20261022: The image gets the CodeQL 2.27.3 bundle, sha256 checked, with the CLI plus its query packs, so a run doesn't download anything. The other languages' extractors are removed, about 500 MB of its 1.4 GB. It's the bundle rather than the bare CLI, since the CLI zip doesn't have any queries.
		- 20261022: Rust in CodeQL has build mode `none` only. Its extractor runs rust-analyzer, which runs cargo, build scripts, and proc macros, but not a full build. Offline it reads the vendored copies through cargo's source replacement.
		- 20261022: The extractor runs `cargo metadata` under Rust 1.99.0 with `rust-src` rather than under the project's 1.96, and fetches that toolchain when it's missing. A run can't, so the image installs it, pinned as `CODEQL_RUST` beside the bundle's version. It wasn't checked whether it requests that exact version or the newest stable, which would break the pin at the next Rust release.
		- 20261022: When the workspace doesn't load, the extractor goes on without types or macros and the database still builds. The analysis then gave 50 `rust/unused-variable` results in our code, such as `None` in a pattern read as a variable, and missed a planted unused variable. So the step fails when the extractor's log says it couldn't load the workspace.
		- 20261022: `cicd/utility/codeql.bash` copies the workspace under `<target>/codeql/src`, runs `cargo vendor --versioned-dirs` into it, and builds the database with the dependencies extracted as source, for x86_64 Linux, default features. Only our crates are indexed as files. A vendored crate's own manifest loaded as a workspace of its own and failed offline, 138 of them.
		- 20261022: Results are limited to the release binary by path rather than by what's extracted. Results in `source/`, `knobs/`, and the vendored crates that `cargo tree -e normal --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` lists, proc macros left out, are kept. Build scripts, proc macros, and dev or build dependencies are still extracted, since cargo needs them, and their results are dropped. That was 191 crates on 20261022.
		- 20261022: The suite is `rust-security-and-quality` rather than the default `rust-code-scanning`. The parent's requirements include correctness checks too, and those are in the quality queries. It's set as `CODEQL_SUITE` in `cicd/config.bash`.
		- 20261022: It runs under the leak checks, after the heap-growth test, so it's on in a full run and off under `--quick` and `--gate`. A run here takes it into the image, like the ASan run, and warns and skips without docker. The SARIF goes to `cicd/artifacts/leakcheck/`, rotated with the heap reports.
		- 20261022: It's opt-in for now. `--codeql` adds the step to the leak checks, so it needs them on too, and `--gate` refuses it. A default full run leaves it out, so the run stays green and short until its cost is settled and its findings are filed under 2026102211462005.
		- 20261022: Measured here, it's slow. The database takes about 5 to 6 minutes. The analysis ran 35 minutes at 8 threads and about 19 GB of memory without finishing, and was stopped: 39 of 41 queries done, `rust/cleartext-logging` (CWE-312) and the summary stats still running. So the step can add well over half an hour to a full run. Whether it goes back in by default is settled on 2026102211462005.

The image was built once, by the gate run.
		- 20261103: The first full measured run, at 595a542 in the image at a load of 8 to 14, took about 65 minutes for the step. That's too slow for every full run, so it stays under `--long` (2026102211462005).

- Test on arm64 macOS in CI
	- ID: 2026102113432600
	- Type: Task
	- Status: Done
	- Priority: Avg
	- Opened: 20261021-123000
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Test environment: GitHub macos-15, arm64
	- Requirements:
		- Runs on any git host that can run a bash script.
		- Free for the public repo.
	- Notes:
		- `cicd/ci-mac.bash` builds, lints, and tests on a Mac. `.github/workflows/mac.yml` checks out and calls it, on pushes to `dev` and `main` and by hand. Another git host only has to run the script.
		- GitHub Actions costs nothing here. Standard hosted runners are free and unlimited on public repos, macOS included. `macos-latest`, `macos-26`, `macos-15`, and `macos-14` are arm64 M1 standard runners, and `macos-15-intel` is the Intel one. Larger runners are always billed. Source: docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners.
		- The 10x macOS minute multiplier that some blog posts mention only draws down a private repo's included minutes. A public repo isn't charged.
		- The Free plan's limits are 5 macOS jobs at once, 20 jobs in all, and 6 hours a job. No rate limit is listed for public repos. GitHub warns that macOS arm64 jobs may queue longer. Source: docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits.
		- The runner is an Apple M1 (Virtual) with 3 cores and 7 GB, on macOS 15.7. `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType` doesn't print anything there.
		- wgpu finds a Metal adapter named "Apple Paravirtual device", reported as an integrated GPU, so GPU tests run. GitHub's docs say Metal Performance Shaders aren't supported, which didn't matter here. There are 2 tests that skip, for the missing software adapter and the missing Metal allocator report.
		- A run takes 4 to 6 minutes: build 100 s, clippy 55 s, and tests 185 s.
		- Found along the way:
			- rustup 1.28 and later doesn't install the toolchain in `rust-toolchain.toml` by itself. Run `rustup toolchain install <channel> --profile minimal --component clippy` first, and set `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN`, so the cross targets the file lists aren't downloaded.
			- `bash` on PATH is Apple's 3.2. Tests that need bash 4.4 fail with `bad substitution`. `brew install bash` takes about 6 s on the runner and gives 5.3, so it goes first on PATH.
			- `cargo test -- --nocapture` doesn't leave any failure text. The script runs the failed tests again alone to get it.
			- Cargo fetches glyphon, alacritty, shcl, and x11-clipboard from github.com. A move to another git host means changing those URLs too.
			- `actions/checkout@v4` prints a Node.js 20 deprecation notice. It still works.
		- Launching the app in a window wasn't tested.
		- To reuse this in another project, copy the script and the workflow. The script reads the toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml`, and uses `--about` for the adapter.
	- Branch: macci
	- Commit: ba66aed
	- Test case: Not applicable. The script was made to fail on a planted test failure, and exited 1 with the failed tests named.
	- Closed: 20261021-134326

- Settings|Window: New option, disabled by default: "On text zoom change window size too".
	- ID: 2026101816103602
	- Type: Enhancement
	- Status: Done
	- Needs external testing: A look on Windows, macOS, and a Wayland desktop: a zoom in to the screen edge and back, and a zoom on a window snapped on Windows, which should keep its size.
	- Priority: Avg
	- Opened: 20261018-161036
	- Opened by: JC
	- Target OS: All
	- Notes:
		- Pre-next-cut.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261019: This is a best guess, since the question of what "change window size too" means went unanswered, and it's easy to reverse. With it on, a zoom in, out, or reset resizes the window so each pane keeps its columns and rows. It stops at the right and bottom edges of the work area on the window's monitor, and past them the grid gets smaller as it does today.
		- The row is "Resize window on zoom" on the Window tab, under "Remember maximized". The setting is `window.resize_on_zoom`, off by default, so nothing changes until it's turned on.
		- The panes' grids are kept rather than the window's. The minimap is fixed in pixels, so keeping the window's grid gave the shell an extra column at each step in.
		- The window grows right and down from where it is, and is never moved. Zooming back to where a run of zooms began puts back the size it had then.
		- A maximized or fullscreen window keeps its size. So does one snapped on Windows. A Wayland compositor refuses a tiled window's resize by itself. X11 and macOS don't say when a window is tiled, so there it resizes.
		- The size saved after a zoom is the one the zoom requested, saved for the monitor as with any zoom. Each window reads the setting when it zooms, so a change in Settings applies to every open window.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261019: Done. A zoom requests the smallest size, in whole cells, that gives each pane its grid. A zoom in a row keeps the grids from before the first one, until the window is resized some other way, the font changes, or a pane is split.
	- Verified: On X11 with xfwm4, with a window at 80x24 and the minimap, each zoom in kept the shell at 70x24 (71 at some steps) up to the screen edge, then the grid shrank. A zoom back and a reset gave back the first size, and the saved size went back to 80x24. With the setting off the window kept its size. A maximized window kept its size, and a split pane kept its grid. The row and its tip were checked at a 24 pt interface font. The unit tests, and clippy for Linux, Windows, and macOS, pass.
	- Swept: Every way to zoom goes through the 2 changed functions, including the keys, the View menu, and the macOS menu. The setting is in the config template, its reader, the dialog spec, and every key list, and the dialog's completeness tests pass.
	- Branch: zoomsize
	- Commit: e5f8a69
	- Test case: de5d1 `a_zoom_grows_the_window_only_to_the_work_area_edge`, de5d2 `a_zoom_keeps_to_its_own_monitor_and_its_grid`, de5d3 `a_zoom_resizes_the_window_only_when_turned_on`.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the change does what the item asked, read as recorded under Decisions, and its tests and the X11 checks pass.
	- Closed: 20261019-105453

- Move local CICD steps into a local container, and on the other boxes too?
	- ID: 2026101009221201
	- Type: Task
	- Status: Done
	- Priority: Avg
	- Opened: 20261010-092212
	- Opened by: JC
	- Target OS: All
	- Requirements:
		- What would you think of moving (or recreating) local CICD steps into a local container (in the regular docker location)? A minimal container, maybe something as close to the current host OS as possible? (E.g. Debian Trixie)? Ditto on foreign boxes?
	- Notes:
		- Pre-next-cut.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261010: A: Yes for the Linux stages that don't need a card or a desktop: lint, unit tests, the 4 builds, the deb and NSIS packages, and the Xvfb and headless sway window tests. They gain a pinned toolchain (rustup 1.96, zig 0.16, mingw, makensis 3.12 instead of the box's 3.11), no live user config under the unit tests (G6), and no writes to the box's cache or dogfood config. Debian Trixie matches the host kernel. The repo, `target/`, and the cargo registry go in as volumes, so build time stays the same.
			- Keep on the host: anything that reads the real card (GPU memory, frame times, the profiler), the dogfood install into the synced app dir, the demo render, and the stages that talk to the other boxes over ssh with the host lock.
			- It doesn't go on the other boxes. vm925w has its hypervisor off, so it can't run WSL2 or Windows containers, and the Windows tests need a logged-on desktop anyway. On b26 a Linux container doesn't help a macOS build, and the Windows and Mac builds are already made here.
			- Suggested first step: `cicd.bash --gate` inside the container, as an opt-in flag, until it has run clean a few times. Then come the package stages.
		- 20261010: It was built after "ok do the container work". `cicd.bash --container` runs stages 1 to 6 in the image from `cicd/container/Dockerfile`, with `--gate --container` for the gate alone. The image has Debian trixie, the pinned rustc with its 3 cross targets, the 4 cargo helpers, zig, makensis 3.12 from the snapshot archive, pwsh with PSScriptAnalyzer, ruff, mypy, shellcheck 0.11, Xvfb, xfwm4, sway, cage, and Mesa. Versions come from `tool-pins.txt` and `rust-toolchain.toml` as build args, and the tag hashes the recipe plus those, so a pin bump is a new image. The run inside has its own target dir, `target/container`, and a named cache volume. Outside, this box runs the sync first and the private runner, dogfood, demo, and publish after, plus the content scrub and the Windows scenarios, which the run inside skips. shellcheck, ruff, and mypy joined the pin list, and the pin probe reads the first version anywhere in a tool's output, since shellcheck's is on its second line.
		- 20261010: These were the first runs. The gate passed inside once the run got a passwd entry for its uid, since the terminal looks its user up. A full run then found 3 more gaps, fixed in turn: the publish test wanted rar on PATH even with the backup off (its own stub rar is on PATH now), xfwm4 needs a session bus (the run inside gets one from dbus-run-session), and the ARM64 Windows exe needs llvm-windres for its icon (llvm-19 is in the image). Inside, every window test but the one that needs a render node runs. That one skips, as on any box without a GPU. The image is 5 GB and takes about 20 minutes to build the first time.
		- 20261010: Run 4 got to the Windows resource check and stopped there again. llvm-windres preprocesses the .rc with clang, so clang-19 was added to the recipe. Everything before that passed inside, both scroll harness arms and the 4 release builds included. It wasn't run again yet, and work stopped at noon.
		- 20261013: This branch has dev merged in. The full run `cicd.bash --container -y --no-publish --no-dogfood --no-private` passes at a2d83b1. Its log is `target/container/run7_20261013-064920.log`, and the copy the run keeps is `cicd/artifacts/lint/run_20261013-064920.log`. The image with clang-19 built in about 9 minutes, with docker's cache warm.
			- Run 5 stopped in the test run folder test, on 2 checks the live settings work broke rather than the container. The socket test bound a path past the 107-byte limit, and the check for code asking for the temp dir didn't know that code moved to `peers.rs`. Both are fixed. The socket test failed before the fix and passes after, with the long folder name.
			- The run inside now gets this box's time zone. Names it stamped, such as test folders and flamegraphs, were in UTC and sorted after the ones made here.
			- Inside, every window test passes, the new live settings one too, except the one that needs a render node, which skips as before. The Windows scenarios ran here after the container and skipped, since the console session was locked.
			- The packages stage makes the same 12 files as the 10-09 run on this box: 4 binaries, 2 deb, 2 rpm, 2 installers, the sums, and built-from.txt. Each is about 1% bigger, in line with the code added since. makensis inside is 3.12. Each package contains the exact binary that run built.
			- It's waiting on UAT, since it changes how the pipeline runs. It isn't merged into dev.
	- Branch: container
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/container/run.bash` (ddrp2): the tag, the recipe against the pins, the option split, the artifacts picked up, and the engine against a stand-in docker, the time zone included. The full run above.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: `--container` is opt-in, so the host run is unchanged. The full run inside passed and made the same packages, and the container test passes on dev at 07f3f6a.
	- Closed: 20261013-105632

	- Progress log:
		- 20261013: Q: Which font settings does a theme hold, and does picking a theme change them? A: Font family, size and line height (`font.family`, `font.size`, `font.line_height_scale`), picked up like the colors. Plus a new switch, on by default: "Font settings ignore themes". While it is on, a theme pick leaves the fonts alone.
		- 20261013: It's built. A saved theme keeps the 3 values under `themes.<slug>.font`, and a pick sets them while the new switch is off.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261013: The font rows stay out of the theme's preset group. As members they would show the default font under any built-in theme, and the person's own font only under Custom.
		- 20261013: A pick sets each theme value that differs from what shows, the way typing it in would, so "Use system font" turns off for that value and the theme's font wins. A value already showing is left alone, so Save, which picks the theme again, doesn't turn anything off.
		- 20261013: Built-in themes don't have a font. Picking one, or Custom, never changes the font.
		- 20261013: Save and Save as always keep the font on screen, switch on or off, since a theme is stored whole.
		- 20261013: With the switch off, a font that differs from the saved theme's makes the box read `Name *`, enables Save, and is named in the tip, like a color. Nothing records it. Turning the switch off doesn't set a font until the next pick.
		- 20261013: The switch is `font.ignore_themes`, one row on the Themes tab under Mode, rather than repeated on the Text tab.
		- 20261013: Theme files from before this don't have font lines. They load as before, and picking one doesn't change the font.
	- Swept: every theme pick goes through `fields::set` or `fields::reset` on the Theme row: the dropdown, Save, Save as, Delete, and the reset arrow. Rename isn't a pick. Nothing outside the dialog picks a theme. `read_user_themes` and `write_user_themes` are the only theme file reader and writer, and all 4 places that build a `UserTheme` set its font.

- The event loop does blocking work on every pass
	- ID: 2026100314050005
	- Type: Enhancement
	- Status: Done
	- Needs local test suite run?: No
	- Needs external testing: macOS on b26: the menu bar still follows a hotkey rebinding and a View menu state change (fullscreen, Read only), and isn't rebuilt while nothing changes.
		- Verified 20261007 on b26 at 107b8e6: the menu bar follows a hotkey moved in the `keys:` block, and the Read only and fullscreen checks. Sampled during 7 s of typing, the menu bar was never rebuilt.
	- Priority: Avg
	- Opened: 20261003-140500
	- Opened by: CC
	- Target OS: All
	- Requirements:
		- Nothing that waits on the X server, reads the environment, or builds strings runs on every `about_to_wait` pass.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261003: `freeze_sync` runs on every pass and every redraw. Its `hidden()` calls `is_minimized()`, which on X11 is a property request that waits for its reply.
		- 20261003: `idle_rule` reads `SILK_IDLE_SECS` twice per pass through `release_deadline`. The file's own note at `env_flag` says to read the environment once.
		- 20261003: on macOS, `bar_menus_key` reads the fullscreen state and builds a string per hotkey on every pass.
		- 20261003: `monitor.rs` opens a new X11 connection in `x11_monitor_under` and again in `button_held`. That runs every 250 ms during a window drag.
		- 20261003: Measured with output every 16 ms: `freeze_sync` took 240 to 275 us a call and was most of a pass's own time outside the frame (283 to 538 us). With an idle window and the cursor animating, it took 61 us a call.
		- 20261003: winit's X11 backend doesn't send anything when a window is minimized, since it never reads `_NET_WM_STATE` changes or unmap. A minimize with focus gives `Focused(false)`, but one without focus doesn't give any event at all. A restore gives `Focused`, `Occluded(false)`, and a redraw.
		- 20261003: Done: the minimized answer is kept for 250 ms and dropped on focus, occlusion, resize, and redraw events, so a restore is still seen at once and the WM's redraw still does the catch-up (G89). The same runs after the fix took 56 to 77 us a call and 93 to 118 us a pass outside the frame, and 26 us a call idle. Those runs draw about 17 frames a second, so at 60 the saving is larger.
		- 20261003: Done: `SILK_IDLE_SECS` is read once per process.
		- 20261003: Done: the macOS menu key hashes the bindings in force directly instead of building a `keys.<name>` string per hotkey. The fullscreen read is winit's own cached flag on macOS rather than a call into AppKit, so it stays.
		- 20261003: The monitor check during a drag was left alone. It costs about 130 us a check, 4 a second, only while a button is held, then once more when the move settles. Keeping a second X connection open for the life of the process would save little.
	- Origin: 6d543d37 (2026-08-30) for `freeze_sync`, 90073855 (2026-09-17) for `idle_rule`, 02482bb7 (2026-10-01) for the menu key, 754c9cb (2026-10-03) for the monitor check. There wasn't an earlier review item. It was plausible when filed, and measured 20261003.
	- Verified: minimize and restore during output, focused and unfocused. A focused minimize froze within 11 ms and an unfocused one within 104 ms. The catch-up frame came 3 ms after the restore. A minimized window still let its device go and got it back on restore. Frame counts matched the old build.
	- Verified: full unit suite passes. Clippy is clean for Linux, Windows, and macOS targets.
	- Swept: every environment read in the source. Only `SILK_PROFILE_OUT`, in profiling builds, is still read per pass. The rest are read once or on a rare event. Every `self.window` state query in app.rs was checked, and no other runs per pass. The rest of the `config_paths()` callers are tests or config reads that don't run per pass.
	- Branch: loopwork
	- Commit: 2e1e8e5
	- Test case: `the_idle_wait_switch_is_read_once` (fails on the old code, passes now), `the_minimized_state_is_asked_at_most_once_per_recheck` (at most 4 asks in a second of 60 passes, and the restore events), `the_bindings_in_force_give_every_hotkey`.
	- Note: Code review 20261003 item 5.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: tested on Linux and b26.
	- Closed: 20261007-093253

- Wallpaper: keep resized copies on disk, oldest pruned first
	- ID: 2026100514211603
	- Type: Enhancement
	- Status: Done
	- Needs local test suite run?: No. The unit tests, clippy for Linux, Windows, and macOS, and the wpresize, wakepic, and new wpkept window tests passed.
	- Needs external testing: The unit tests on vm925w, since a copy is replaced by rename while another process may hold it open. A launch on vm925w and b26, to see the copy written to the platform's cache folder.
		- 20261007: Verified: the unit tests passed on b26 in the full pipeline run at 46a2193.
		- Verified 20261007 on vm925w at 107b8e6: the unit tests passed, and one launch kept its copy in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\silkterm\cache\wallpaper`.
		- Verified 20261007 on b26 at 107b8e6: one launch kept its copy in `~/Library/Caches/silkterm/wallpaper`.
	- Priority: Avg
	- Opened: 20261005-142116
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100418225503, 2026100418225507
	- Target OS: All
	- Requirements:
		- Before RC1.
		- When a window loads or is resized and the original wallpaper is resampled, keep that copy at that size.
		- On a resize, use a kept copy within about 5% of the total pixel count. If there is none, resample the original again and keep that one too.
		- Prune the oldest copies once the cache goes over its size limit.
	- Notes:
		- 20261005: It helps most at launch and when rotation comes back to an image, since both prepare from scratch now. A resize already waits 500 ms after the last change and prepares once.
		- 20261005: The key needs everything that changes the stored pixels: the file and its mtime, the held size, blur, and the look tags.
		- 20261005: A copy is 4 bytes a pixel, so about 14 MB at 2560x1440 unless it's stored compressed. Block compression (2026100418225507) cuts that to a quarter or less.
		- 20261005: Time a release build's prepare first. If it's well under the resize wait, only launch and rotation gain.
		- 20261005: Settled:
			- Store the copies compressed.
			- Waking from resource saving prepares from the file again too, so it gains as well. Item 2026100513581814 is about what shows in the meantime, and both work together.
		- 20261005: How block compression compares with JPEG, or a wavelet format, in size and quality on a blurred picture:
			- It's bigger. BC1 is a fixed 4 bits a pixel and BC7 is 8, so 1/8 and 1/4 of a plain copy. JPEG on a blurred picture is often 1/20 or less, since the blur takes out the fine detail it spends bits on.
			- In quality, BC1 can band on smooth gradients. BC7 and high quality JPEG look like the original. A wavelet format doesn't have any blocks, but JPEG blocks only show at low quality anyway.
			- JPEG and wavelet save disk only. They decode to full size before the upload, which costs time and is a second lossy step. BC stays compressed in graphics memory and uploads without a decode.
			- So if 2026100418225507 is built, keep the BC data on disk, maybe with a general compressor over it. Otherwise use high quality JPEG, since the decoder is already in the build. Time the decode against the prepare first.
		- 20261006: Timed on b23 with a non-LTO optimized build, at the default settings: a prepare took 0.76 to 2.55 s at 1920x1080 and 2560x1440, and 0.41 s at 1280x800. So it's well over the resize wait, and resizes gain too. A JPEG decode of the result took 6 to 24 ms, and reading a kept copy 13 to 33 ms. Writing one took 62 to 118 ms, so it happens after the picture is sent. The full table is in the [reducing resources design doc](design_docs/20261004-182255_reduce-resources.md#kept-copies-on-disk).
		- 20261006: Done: copies are kept as quality 95 JPEG in the platform's cache folder, under a `wallpaper` folder. A `--config` keeps them beside that config. Each copy keeps the original's summary, so derived colors don't move. A copy within 5% is used for the size requested, and the window takes it as that size. Pictures with transparency, and pictures held whole without a blur or mask, aren't kept.
		- 20261006: Light and dark mode aren't in the key, since the mode is applied when the picture is drawn.
		- Verified: unit tests and the wpkept window test pass, and each was seen failing with its part of the feature taken out.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261006: It was built first, as high quality JPEG. Block compression (2026100418225507) stays queued.
		- 20261006: Prune at 256 MB, oldest used first.
	- Branch: wpcache
	- Commit: 34fa3fe
	- Test case: Unit tests ddkhb, ddkhc, ddkhd, ddkhe, ddkhf, ddkhg, ddkhh. Window test `cicd/tests/wpkept/run.bash` (ddkhn) in stage 3.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: tested on Linux, Windows, and macOS.
	- Closed: 20261007-093253

It was at most 5 levels off, but the blocks showed as a grid with the contrast stretched. It would have saved 2 MiB at 2560x1440.
		- 20261007: Done: a picture held by the window goes to the GPU as BC1, an eighth of its plain size. Pictures held by their blur, and any with transparency, stay plain.
		- 20261007: Done: a device without BC gets the picture plain. A BC1 texture is padded to whole 4x4 blocks, and the shader reads only the part that contains the picture.
		- 20261007: Done: the disk cache keeps a BC1 picture as its blocks, so a kept copy doesn't need a decode or encode. A picture held by its blur is still kept as JPEG. Copies in the old format are removed at the next prune.
		- 20261007: Done: on GL the check for a lost wallpaper skips a BC1 picture, since GL can't read a compressed texture back.
		- 20261007: Verified on b23, with a 2560x1440 photo without blur at 2560x1440: the texture went from 14.1 MiB to 1.8. On X11 the wallpaper's share of graphics memory went from 32 MiB to 1, and of regular memory from 46 to 11. On Vulkan the allocator's in-use figure went from 65.5 to 52.4 MiB, and the driver's figure stayed the same.
		- 20261007: Verified: at the default blur, no pixels changed against the build before, dark and light, GL and Vulkan, and memory was the same.
		- 20261007: Verified: without blur, it was under a level off on average. It was at most 6 or 7 on the built-in in dark mode, 12 to 17 in light mode, 32 around small colored stars, and 65 there at 100% visibility without a scrim. A light blur of 2 was at most 4 to 7. An odd window size was no worse at the edges.

The new window checks fail on the build before this.

It was seen on the built-in in light mode on a close look, and plainly with the contrast stretched 4 times. There weren't any contour bands. Is that the banding the BC7 decision was for? Options: keep BC1 as built, BC7 for pictures with little or no blur (twice BC1's size, 3.5 MiB at 2560x1440, and far better on gradients), or keep pictures without blur plain.
