	- Progress log:
		- 20261003: Each `CursorMoved` over a dialog sets it dirty. `dialog.rs` `render` then builds a new glyphon buffer and shapes it for every text item, and rebuilds the rects and texts. A tab with 40 rows shapes 60 to 100 buffers per mouse event.
		- 20261003: `hover_tip` runs twice per render with the same pointer, once for `over` and once for `found`.

	- Actual fix:
		- Shaped text is kept from one frame to the next, found by its text, font, weight, color, and line box. A frame shapes only text the last one didn't have. A move, a new clip, or a new width reuses the shape. A new text context, which a font, size, or scale change makes, starts over.

		- A frame looks up the tip once. A tip coming due, or a field edit's animation step, gets its frame when it's due rather than on every pass of the loop.

	- Verified: 20261004, the unit suite passes, 1112 tests, and the sister item's tests pass unchanged. fmt is clean, clippy is clean for Linux and Windows, and the test ID check passes. It wasn't looked at in a real window.

- When a shcl upgrade breaks the config format, keep the old file and write a new one from scratch
	- ID: 2026100312470546
	- Type: Feature
	- Status: Done
	- Needs external testing: The new unit tests on Windows, at the next vm925w run.
	- Priority: Avg
	- Opened: 20261003-124705
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026100220292612, 2026100315553545
	- Target OS: All
	- Requirements:
		- Before RC1.
		- When wiring a new version of shcl into the code, first see if it has a new API to do the conversion, or at least help with it.
		- Check if the new shcl version has breaking changes. If so:
			- Rename the latest config file `[origname]_backup_YYYYmmDD-HHMMSS_format-v[shcl version].shcl`.
			- Write a new config file with the same path and name as before, from scratch through shcl, using whatever settings and conversions shcl can handle or are salvageable.
		- Future versions of shcl might do the config backup and conversion. Be careful not to race, conflict with, or trample what shcl might do.
	- Notes:
		- 20261003: Item 2026100220292612 already keeps a copy on every format upgrade, as `config_backup_YYYYmmDD-HHMMSS_format-v<N>.shcl`. N is the old file's Format number, which has matched shcl's major version so far. It copies the file and then converts it in place, rather than writing a new one from scratch.
		- 20261003: shcl 3.0's `migrate_unstamped` is the help shcl gives today. It respells a 2.x file, and doesn't make a backup.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261003: Keep the in-place conversion whenever shcl can migrate the file. Write a new file from scratch, keeping what still parses, only when shcl can't read or migrate it. The old file is kept under the name 2026100220292612 already uses, `config_backup_YYYYmmDD-HHMMSS_format-v<N>.shcl`, rather than a second scheme.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261003: shcl b10c2009, and its dev branch at e9e4a6c, have `migrate`, `migrate_unstamped`, and `format_version`, but nothing that converts a whole file or keeps a copy. The CLI's `migrate --write` keeps `config_old_v2.shcl`, but the library doesn't have such a call, so nothing here can race it today.
		- 20261003: A file shcl can't migrate is one that its stamped `migrate` doesn't give a Format line, as for a raw block that never closes. `migrate_unstamped`, the call for a program that writes its own footer, can't report that, so the stamped call is made too. Filed as shcl friction, 2026100315553545.
		- 20261003: A file shcl can't read is one that isn't UTF-8. Before, such a file loaded as all defaults without a message, and a Settings save said it saved but didn't write anything. In an older format it is now written new, and a line that doesn't decode is left out. A current-format file that isn't UTF-8 isn't an upgrade and is left as it was.
		- 20261003: The new file is the template with every setting that still reads copied into it, as the pre-nesting conversion does. Themes, per-monitor sizes, and the shell list are copied too. Each line shcl can't read, and each setting with nowhere to go, counts as lost.
		- 20261003: Lost settings are reported by the same writer, terminal line, and notice as a conversion in place. The text says the file couldn't be converted in place, so a new one was written, and how many settings couldn't be kept. The notice title stays "Settings not converted".
		- 20261003: Before this, a 2.x file with a raw block that never closed was converted in place without a copy kept, since the new footer ended up inside the block and the file never read as a newer format. It now gets a copy and a new file.
		- 20261003: The choice is made in one place, `upgrade` in config.rs, so a later shcl that converts whole files can take it over there.
		- 20261003: README and design.md say what happens to such a file.
	- Verified: The unit suite passes, 1074 tests. fmt is clean, and clippy is clean for Linux, Windows, and macOS. The test ID check passes. With the old behavior put back, the 3 rewrite tests failed, and the pipeline test failed its can't-migrate, can't-read, and notice checks. - At the RC release, convert the config to the new format and keep the old file beside it
	- ID: 2026100220292612
	- Type: Feature
	- Status: Done
	- Needs external testing: A dogfood launch of a release build on a real 2.x config, on Linux and on Windows. On Windows, check that `config_backup_<time>_format-v2.shcl` appears beside the roaming config with the local time in its name, and that a 2.x file with a list in brackets brings up the system message box naming the count and the copy.
	- Priority: Avg
	- Opened: 20261002-202926
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: the old-format item about removing the code that migrates old config files.
	- Target OS: All
	- Test environment: b23
	- Requirements:
		- Upon RC release, convert settings to the new format.
		- Keep the old config file under a suffixed name, still ending in `.shcl`.
		- If any settings can't be salvaged, warn the user.
	- Notes:
		- Today the shcl 3 conversion rewrites the file in place and doesn't keep a copy. Only the older flat-file conversion moves the original aside, to `.bak`.
			- Note: 20261003: The shcl 3 conversion keeps a copy now. See the progress log.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261003: It's built now, and for every format upgrade as well as at RC. A launch that converts the file first copies it to `config.format<N>.shcl` beside it, with N the old format, and never overwrites a copy already there. Settings that can't be kept get a notice at launch.
		- 20261003: Every older version is kept, never one per format. The copy is named `config_backup_YYYYmmDD-HHMMSS_format-v<N>.shcl`, with the time it was made and the format it had. This replaces the `config.format<N>.shcl` name above.
		- 20261003: Settings the conversion can't keep get a warning dialog as well as the terminal message.
		- 20261003: When 2 windows convert the same file in the same second, they may leave one copy, which is acceptable. The notice title stays "Settings not converted".
		- 20261003: A Settings save that converts the file warns only when settings couldn't be converted. A clean conversion stays quiet.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261003: Any write that moves the file to a newer format first copies it to `config.format<N>.shcl` beside it. N is the Format number the file had. A file without a Format line counts as 2, since that's how the conversion reads it. The copy is made in the writer every settings write goes through, so a Settings save that converts a file a busy launch left alone keeps one too.
		- 20261003: A copy already there is never replaced, and the file is still converted. If the copy can't be made, the write is refused. The copy is written under a name of its own and then linked into place, so 2 windows converting at once leave one whole copy. On a filesystem without hard links it's written in place.
		- 20261003: A 2.x line with a list in brackets doesn't have a 3.0 spelling. It stays as written and doesn't set anything, and the launch that converts prints the count and where the copy is. Unreadable lines and unknown keys were already reported at every launch, so those are left to that.
		- 20261003: The footer refresh no longer puts the Format line on a file still in 2.x spellings. A file whose conversion was put off could get the line without the respelling, and then never convert.
		- 20261003: The flat pre-nesting conversion keeps its `.bak`. It's a layout change and doesn't have a format number. A flat file doesn't have a Format line, so the 2.x step that runs before it already keeps the untouched original as `config.format2.shcl`.
		- 20261003: README and design.md say where the copy goes.
		- 20261003: The copy is now `config_backup_YYYYmmDD-HHMMSS_format-v<N>.shcl`, replacing the `config.format<N>.shcl` name above. The time is local, as the test folders and the pipeline's log names are. A file named by `--config` uses its own name, less any `.shcl`, in place of `config`: `mine.shcl` keeps `mine_backup_..._format-v2.shcl`, and `mine.conf` keeps `mine.conf_backup_..._format-v2.shcl`.
		- 20261003: Every conversion makes a new copy, and none is ever replaced. The link-or-fail step stays. A name already taken in the same second moves on to `_2` before the `.shcl`, then `_3`, and so on. A name whose file has the same bytes counts as the same copy, so 2 windows converting the same file at once still leave one.
		- 20261003: Settings the conversion can't keep now also get the notice window a refused save uses, once the terminal is on screen. Titled "Settings not converted", it names the file, says how many settings couldn't be converted and now do nothing, and gives the copy's name in the same folder. Windows shows the same text in the system message box. The terminal line is unchanged apart from the new name.
		- 20261003: A Settings save that converts a file a busy launch left alone keeps a copy, but says nothing about lost settings, on the terminal or in a notice. That was already so before.
		- 20261003: `a_copy_already_there_is_left_as_it_was` (dder0) is reworked as `a_second_conversion_keeps_a_second_copy`, since a copy already there no longer stops a new one. `every_settings_write_goes_through_the_restore` now looks for the publish in `write_config_keeping`, which `write_config_atomic` calls, so the one writer still names it once.
		- 20261003: Settings the conversion can't keep are now reported by the writer every settings write goes through, rather than by the launch step. So a Settings save that converts a file a busy launch left alone gives the same terminal line and the same "Settings not converted" notice, with the count and the copy. A clean conversion doesn't say anything. The launch reports it the same way as before.
		- 20261003: The count is read from the copy, which is the file as it was. The window takes it from its event loop as for a launch, so the notice comes up once, in the window that wrote.
		- 20261003: Each write path was checked. A Settings save, a window or font size save, a menu toggle, and a shell list update all go through `persist`, which converts a file a launch left alone, so each reports a loss. The default shell move reads the file the same way and reports too. The rating write, revert, clear, backfill, migrate, and the wallpaper repair write the text as it was read and never convert. The pre-nesting conversion runs after the 2.x step, so it finds the file converted already. A new file and a PowerShell profile don't have anything to convert.
		- 20261003: The pipeline test for old config files passed (2026100313404573), which closes this item.
	- Note: Launch notices go to the terminal, like every other launch message about the file. A desktop launch or a Windows release build doesn't show any of them.
		- Note: 20261003: Settings the conversion can't keep are the exception now, with a notice window too.
	- Verified: The unit suite passes, 1021 tests. fmt and clippy are clean for Linux and for the Windows target. The test ID and markdown checks pass. With the copy turned off, the launch and refusal tests failed. With the copy written in place instead of linked, the race test saw a part copy in 3 runs out of 3. Without the footer guard, the footer test failed.
		- 20261003: The unit suite passes, 1057 tests. fmt is clean, and clippy is clean for Linux, Windows, and macOS. The test ID, markdown, and table checks pass. With a taken name counted as done, the second-copy and same-second tests failed. With same bytes not counted as the same copy, the same-second and race tests failed. With the loss not handed to the window, the notice test failed. Without hard links, the race test saw a part copy in 3 runs out of 3.
		- 20261003: Seen on Linux: a launch on a 2.x `--config mine.shcl` with a list in brackets made `mine_backup_<time>_format-v2.shcl` and put the notice up over the terminal after its first frame. The next launch didn't make a copy or show a notice.
		- 20261003: On vm925w at 8877157, on NTFS, a lone `cargo test` passed, 1035 tests. These copy tests passed by name: `a_launch_keeps_the_2x_file_beside_the_converted_one`, `a_second_conversion_keeps_a_second_copy`, `copies_made_in_one_second_never_replace_each_other`, `launches_converting_at_once_leave_one_whole_copy`, `the_footer_never_stamps_a_2x_file`, `a_setting_the_conversion_cannot_keep_is_reported`, `a_launch_that_loses_a_setting_leaves_a_notice_for_the_window`, and `every_settings_write_goes_through_the_restore`. `a_write_that_cannot_keep_the_old_file_is_refused` is Unix only, so it doesn't run there.
		- 20261003: The unit suite passes, 1059 tests. fmt is clean, and clippy is clean for Linux, Windows, and macOS. The test ID and markdown checks pass. With the loss reported only by the launch step again, the new save test failed, but the launch test still passed.
	- Swept: Every settings write goes through `write_config_atomic`. The only other moves of the file are `--reset-config` and the move from the old config folder, and neither changes the format. PowerShell profile writes go through the same writer but don't have a Format line, so they never get a copy.
		- 20261003: No `format2` or `.format<N>` name is left in the code, README, or design.md. The local-time stamp is one function now, shared with the test folder. The notice is put up only in `show_notice`, and `take_conversion_loss` is read only in the window's event loop.

- A unit test run on macOS or Windows could import and rename the box's own `~/.config/silkterm/config.toml`
	- ID: 2026111018340691
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261110-183406
	- Opened by: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026110920480399
	- Target OS: macOS, Windows
	- Reproduced: No. It was found by reading config.rs. Linux doesn't take the `~/.config` fallback, so it can't show here.
		- 20261110: Today's tests can't reach it. Every test that points the settings at a file of its own does it through `set_config_override`, which also sets the release build's override, and with that set there is no `~/.config` path at all. So only that side effect kept it safe.
	- Possible cause: Under cfg(test), `may_write` checks only the native path. `beta1_config_paths` adds `legacy_config_path()`, built from the real HOME, so a test whose own folder has no settings file would read a real beta1 file there and rename it. `adopt_legacy_config` may have the same gap.
	- Actual cause: The test build's write check guarded only the file being written, not the old file being moved away, and didn't count `~/.config/silkterm` as the box's own folder off Linux. `adopt_legacy_config` had the same gap.
	- Actual fix: In a test build, a pre-layout or beta1 file in the box's own folder is never moved or renamed, and `~/.config/silkterm` counts as the box's folder on every platform. A release build is unchanged.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261110: The test uses the stand-in for the box's folder that ddgbt uses, rather than HOME at a temp folder. HOME is process-global, and the tests that read the box's own settings run beside it. It calls the 2 moves directly with that folder's files, since a whole load doesn't take a `~/.config` path on Linux.
	- Branch: rnd1111b
	- Test case: `a_test_run_never_moves_an_old_config_from_the_boxs_folder` (df4we). It fails with the 3 guards taken out (the old shcl file moved) and passes with them.
	- Verified: The backlog quick run passes in all 5 areas, with 1466 unit tests.
	- Swept: Every rename or removal of a file the program didn't just write in config.rs: `adopt_legacy_config`, `import_beta1_config`, and `keep_beta1_config`, which renames only what the import read. The other renames and removals in config.rs are of the settings file itself, its backups, or temp files a save made beside it, all in the folder the write check already covers.
	- Closed: 20261110-190049

- A notice can wrap one more line at 2x than at 1x
	- ID: 2026111014301817
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261110-143018
	- Opened by: CC
	- Target OS: All
	- Test environment: b23, CPU text layout in the unit tests.
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- In `refusal_notice` in `dialog.rs`, make the second paragraph "Until that is fixed, changes such as the window size, new shells, and anything set in Settings are used now but not kept."
		- Run `about_and_the_notice_lay_out_again_at_twice_the_size` (dd5nh).
	- Incorrect behavior: The notice is 234 high at 1x and 521 at 2x, a ratio of 2.23, so a line that fits at 1x wraps at 2x.
	- Expected behavior: A notice wraps the same at any scale, so its size scales with it.
	- Reproduced: Yes, 20261110. The same sentence without the comma before "and", or with "used but not kept", lays out at about 2x.
	- Possible cause: Text widths at 2x aren't exactly double the 1x widths, and the wrap width is, so a line close to the edge at 1x doesn't fit at 2x.
	- Notes:
		- The notice text was changed to "used but not kept" so dd5nh passes. The test passes or fails on where the words fall, rather than on the layout rule.
	- Actual cause: The UI font size is rounded to a whole pixel at each scale, 17 at 1x and 35 at 2x here, so text at 2x measured 2.06 times its 1x width. The wrap width was the scale factor times 440, exactly double.
	- Actual fix: A notice, the tmux question, and a menu tip wrap at a width that follows the UI font as drawn, from the new `TextCtx::ui_text_dip`. At 1x it's the width as written, so nothing changes there. design.md's "Measurements and display scaling" says so.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261110: The notice keeps "used but not kept". It was picked in the wording pass, and the layout no longer depends on it.
		- 20261110: The wrap width follows the font, rather than the font being made exactly double. A rounded font size keeps text sharp, and only the wrap decision needed to match.
	- Swept: every word wrap against a fixed width: `wrap_paras` (notice and tmux question) and the menu tip in `app/menus.rs`. The Settings and About tips wrap to the window's width, which isn't a fixed width, and were left alone.
	- Verified: 20261110. With the issue's sentence in `refusal_notice`, dd5nh failed (234 -> 521) before the fix and passed after. df4rf and df4rg failed with the old wrap width and pass now. The quick run passes in all 5 areas.
	- Branch: rnd1111
	- Test case: `a_notice_wraps_at_the_same_words_at_any_scale` (df4rf) and `text_fitted_to_a_ui_width_wraps_the_same_at_any_scale` (df4rg), at 1.25, 1.5, 2 and 3 against 1x. dd5nh, unchanged.
	- Closed: 20261110-165318

- Settings: Side-tabs: the lower the tab, the lower the text is within the tab
	- ID: 2026110609500003
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261106-095000
	- Opened by: JC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Notes:
		- Pre-next-cut.
	- Reproduced: No, 20261106. On Xvfb at scales 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, and 2, and under headless sway on the RTX 3060 Ti at 1, 1.25, and 2, every tab's title sits the same distance above its box's bottom edge, sub-tabs included. A dev debug build and the 11-01 release build read the same.
	- Progress log:
		- 20261106: The title's height comes from its own tab's box, the same box that is drawn, so nothing in the layout can add up down the list. Both renderers in the frame get the same surface size.
		- 20261109: Measured the tabs from Silk down to Keys. Every box is 29 px tall, and every baseline sits 8 px above the box's bottom edge, so nothing moves down the list. The letters are what differ. A title with a tall letter (Silk, Themes, Background, Window, Shell) starts 8 px below the box top. A title without one (Appearance, Text, Cursor, Movement, Program, Keys) starts 11 px down, so it looks low. The titles are centered from the top of a tall letter to the baseline, the same as the main window's menu and tab titles.
		- 20261110: Titles now center on their capitals, with the baseline on a whole pixel. In a 29 px box that leaves 9 px over the capitals and 10 under the baseline on every tab, where it was 8 or 11 over before, by letter. A font with a deep descent makes the tabs taller, so g and y stay 2 px clear of the edge.
	- Actual cause [Bug]: Titles were centered by line box, then dropped half the descent, which centers ascender-top to baseline. A title without a tall letter read low.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: Tab titles are placed by their capitals, baseline = band top + (band height + cap height) / 2, snapped to a whole pixel. The band grows when the font leaves less than its descent plus 2 px under the baseline.
	- Test case: `a_tab_title_sits_as_low_in_its_box_on_every_tab` (deyxd) runs on both sides, at 4 scales, in tall and short windows. It fails when a title is moved a quarter pixel per tab. It passes on the current build. `chrome_caps_center_in_bar_on_a_whole_pixel` (df452) and `band_floor_clears_descenders` (df453) fail when the snap or the descent room is taken out.
	- Branch: rnd1106, tabcap
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the new placement was checked in the dialog against the 11-09 build, and its tests fail without it.
	- Closed: 20261110-064500

- knobs' spec checks let a relation loop, case-only twins, a NaN range, and a text chooser through
	- ID: 2026110919171131
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261109-191711
	- Opened by:
	- Related IDs: tukzmon:2026110709074419
	- Steps to reproduce: Load a spec with any of the 4 cases below.
	- Incorrect behavior: Each parses clean. A loop through a setting's auto switch, its rule's state value, or its group's chooser overflows the stack at the first read. Paths that differ only in case pass, and shcl folds them onto one key, so a round trip loses a value. Dropdown options that differ only in case pass, and the second can't be picked. A NaN range end or detent passes, and then every number is in range. A group chooser of type text takes any text as a pick.
	- Expected behavior: Each is refused when the spec loads. Spec::valid also refuses a NaN value, since its range check lets one past.

	- Actual effort: Low
	- Progress log:

		- 20261109: Ported. The Presets and Indent enums weren't needed here, since the chooser check keys on from_program as the rest of check_links does.
	- Actual fix [Bug]: check_links folds case on paths, refuses NaN range ends and detents, refuses option twins, refuses a chooser that isn't a choice, and walks the reads Model::value makes for a loop. Spec::valid refuses a NaN value.
	- Branch: rnd1109
	- Test case: df3k1 to df3k4 in knobs/src/tests.rs. Each fails on the old code. The settings spec and its dialog tests still pass.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the spec checks have tests that fail without them, and the real settings spec still loads.

	- Origin: Found in tukzmon's copy of knobs by its 2026-11-07 code review. The same checks are missing here, in check_links in knobs/src/lib.rs.

	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the cause was made to happen on purpose, and the fix stops it.
	- Closed: 20261109-210500

		- It was found while working on 2026110613085833. That fix didn't cause it. The window it opens at is still 914 DIP tall, 1371 pixels at 1.5, which was past the screen before the fix too.
		- 20261106: Under sway the title bar is still a few pixels off the top, 6 at 1.5 and 2 at 1.25. Sway centers the window without its title bar, so half the room left for it goes below. The window and its title bar together fit the output.
	- Actual cause: the caps asked only the dialog which monitor it was on. On Wayland a window can't say until it's shown on an output, so it didn't have one at open or at the first scale change. At open the scale is also still 1, so a cap from the monitor's pixels would still be too tall.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261106: The terminal's monitor is noted when a dialog opens, in logical pixels by the terminal's scale, and turned into the dialog's pixels by its own scale. A Wayland output reports only a whole number for a scale of 1.5.
		- 20261106: Before the dialog is placed, the terminal's monitor comes first on every platform, since the dialog's own answer is for wherever the origin is. After, the dialog's own comes first, since it may have been dragged to another monitor. The work area keeps its old order.
	- Actual fix: Settings' caps take the terminal's monitor when the dialog can't name its own, or hasn't been placed yet. Under sway at 1.5 it opens 762 tall at scale 1 and stays 762 tall at 1.5 (1143 pixels), where the window was 800 tall with its title bar off the top before.
	- Swept: every call that measures a monitor for a dialog. `settings_caps` was the only one. About and the notice aren't capped. The other `current_monitor` calls are for the terminal window, which is shown before it asks.
	- Verified: 20261106, under headless sway on the GPU with one 1600 x 1200 output. At 1.5 Settings is 762 logical pixels tall where it was 800, and at 1.25 922 where it was 936. At 1 it's 914, its content's size, as before. dez6a fails with the old choice put back and passes with the fix. The dialog unit tests and the quick gate pass.
	- Branch: rnd1107
	- Test case: `a_dialog_that_cannot_name_its_monitor_goes_by_the_terminals` (dez6a).
	- Closed: 20261106-175907

- Settings at scale 1.25 on a short screen: the vertical scrollbar pushes in a horizontal one and cuts off the revert arrows
	- ID: 2026110613085833
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Priority: Low
	- Opened: 20261106-130858
	- Opened by:
	- Target OS: All
	- Reproduced: 20261106, under headless sway at 1.25 on a 1600 x 1200 output. Settings opened 1046 x 1143 pixels where its content wanted 1082 x 1170, so it scrolled both ways and the revert arrows were cut off. At 1x it fits.
	- Actual cause: on Wayland the window opens at scale 1, sized to its content there, and learns the real scale after. The window keeps its DIP size through the change, but the content measures about 3% larger at 1.25, so it was left short on both sides. The height cap wasn't involved, and the vertical scrollbar is in the panel's margin, so it doesn't take any width from the rows.
	- Progress log:
		- It was seen under headless sway at 1.25 with a 960 DIP tall screen, where the dialog opens with its height capped. At 1x on the same setup it fits. It was found while working on 2026110609500003.
		- It may be the expected result of the height cap. Check whether the content width should leave room for the scrollbar.
		- 20261106: The first note's guess was off. The height wasn't capped. The cap came out 1262.5 pixels at 1.25. The new Wayland cap bug is 2026110617385295.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261106: The fix goes in the scale change rather than the snap. The snap only settles within 12 DIP of the natural size, which a scale change can pass, and widening it would catch sizes the user dragged to.
	- Actual fix: after a scale change, a window that was at its content's size, or at the cap that kept it under that, requests the content's size at the new scale, capped again. Each side is judged on its own. A size the user dragged to is kept, and a maximized window is left to the window manager.
	- Swept: every place the Settings window asks for a size. Open uses the content's size at the scale it opens at, and the snap and a resize already round up. About and the notice lay out again on a scale change and ask for their new size.
	- Verified: under headless sway at 1.25 on the GPU, Settings now opens at its content's size, without scrollbars and with every revert arrow in view. At 1.5 the width fits and only the height scrolls, limited by the output (2026110617385295). The dialog unit tests and the quick gate pass.
	- Branch: rnd1107
	- Test case: `a_window_on_its_natural_size_takes_the_new_one_after_a_scale_change` (dez60). It failed with the fix taken out.
	- Closed: 20261106-174100

- Test run folders pile up in HOST_TEMP/silkterm, and the 2-day sweep doesn't take them
	- ID: 2026110514393095
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261105-143930
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: b23
	- Incorrect behavior: On 11-05 there were 28 run folders from 11-01 to 11-04, most with only `.test_silkterm_owner` and `run.pid`. Folders from 11-02 were still there after the 11-04 default run.
	- Expected behavior: Each run removes its folder at the end, and a run removes ones older than 2 days.
	- Reproduced: No. On 11-05 the scroll harness run by hand and the engine harness each left a folder now and then, but not every time.
		- 20261106: Yes. The scroll harness run alone without a binary skips, and leaves a folder with only those 2 files every time. The engine harness didn't leave any in 43 runs.
	- Notes:
		- Which tests leave them isn't known yet.
	- Actual cause:
		- A lone run that skipped (exit 3) or failed kept its folder. The scroll and engine harnesses, and others, remove their own work folder first, so what was kept contained only the owner mark and `run.pid`.
		- The stale sweep ran only in a default or full run, and backlog runs mostly use `--backlog-run-quick`. On 11-06 the sweep would have taken the 8 left from 11-03 and 11-04, but no such run had happened.
		- A read-only folder a test made (ddazx's locked bases) stopped the guard's `rm -rf` partway, after it took `run.pid`. The sweep never saw that folder again (`20261101-140811_001`).
	- Actual fix:
		- The test helpers (`_testdir.bash`, `.py`, `testdir.rs`) remove the folder on a skip too, and on a failure when nothing but the 2 marks is in it. `_testdir.ps1` has the second.
		- `saferm.bash` and `saferm.py` open a read-only folder before removing, so the whole tree is removed.
		- `--backlog-run-quick` sweeps stale run folders too, outside the container.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261106: Exit 3 is the tests' skip code, so a skip removes its folder like a pass. A failed run's folder with any file in it still stays, per 2026103115564575.
		- 20261106: `_testdir.ps1` takes only the empty folder rule, since no PowerShell test uses 3 for a skip. `saferm.ps1` and install.ps1's copy are left as they are, since no PowerShell test makes a read-only folder.
		- 20261106: The quick run sweeps too, per `Temp files`' "each run", as `cicd-win.ps1` already does. It's one listing of one folder.
		- 20261106: de5e9's lone failing run writes a file now, since one with nothing but its marks is removed at once. Before, it didn't write anything.
	- Verified: 20261106. ddazx passes (104 checks), and its 4 new cases failed 8 times against the old helpers and guards. de5e9 passes, with HOST_TEMP set and unset, and its 3 new checks failed against the old guard and `cicd.bash`. dde3v passes under pwsh, and its 2 new checks failed against the old `_testdir.ps1`. When the scroll harness was run alone without a binary, it left a folder with the old helper but not with the new one. `--backlog-run-quick` passed every area, and its end line said it removed 8 stale run folders, the ones from 11-03 and 11-04.
		- Swept: every copy of the helper (`_testdir.bash`, `.py`, `.ps1`, `testdir.rs`) and of the guard (`saferm.bash`, `.py`, `.ps1`, install.ps1's), every bash and Python caller of the helper for an end that calls `fTestDir_End` or `end()`, and every place `cicd.bash` sweeps stale run folders.
		- When de5e9 was run alone without HOST_TEMP, it left its own folder too, since it sourced the guard again after its TMPDIR moved. It sources it first now.
	- Branch: rnd1107
	- Test case: ddazx (`cicd/tests/testdir/run.bash`, its skip, empty, and read-only cases), de5e9 (`cicd/tests/cleanup/run.bash`), dde3v (`cicd/tests/testdir/remove.ps1`), dez6x in `testdir.rs`.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: the tests fail against the old helpers, guard, and pipeline.
	- Closed: 20261106-182548

- deqx1's "xfwm4's window has gone from the X server" sometimes fails on a busy box
	- ID: 2026110318260287
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261103-182602
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026110116413708, 2026110220294255, 2026110319081175
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Steps to reproduce: Run `cicd/tests/herdback/run.bash` 4 times side by side at a load over 20.
	- Incorrect behavior: xfwm4's process is gone, and passes "xfwm4 has stopped", but its `_NET_SUPPORTING_WM_CHECK` window is still on the X server 3 s later. It failed 1 run of 7 on 20261103, at load 25. Every other check in that run passed.
	- Expected behavior: The X server lets go of the window once xfwm4 has exited.
	- Possible cause: Not known. Either the X server is slow to see the closed connection at that load, and the 3 s wait in fGone is short, or something else has xfwm4's connection open, such as a helper started under its dbus-run-session. The kept folder from that run didn't have anything more in its logs.
	- Reproduced: 20261103, from a desktop shell. Once stopped, xfwm4 was running again on the test's display, started by the desktop's own session, and stayed up through the cases without a window manager. Under load, 4 stops in 90 left the window there for good.
	- Actual cause: xfwm4 joined the desktop's xfce4-session through SESSION_MANAGER, and the session starts its window manager again when it exits. The new xfwm4 took the client slot the old one freed, so its check window had the same ID. fGone found it whenever the new one was up before fGone's first look, which a busy box allows. The X server was never slow.
		- With xfwm4 gone and not restarted, the back case without a window manager failed. winit counts a move only from the notice a window manager sends, so the window never knew it was herded. The restarted xfwm4 had sent it.
	- Actual fix: The test's X programs run without SESSION_MANAGER, as gui-headless.bash's do. Without a window manager, the test's moves send the window that notice as a window manager would (`_wmmove.py`), and the key after a move goes to a window it has given focus first, since without focus the key never arrived. A new check fails when a window manager is back on the display for the cases without one.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261103: The moves without a window manager tell the window, rather than staying plain moves. Every window manager sends that notice, so a plain move tests a case that doesn't happen. The herd move doesn't get a key, since a window manager's herd doesn't bring one, and the look after it runs anyway.
		- 20261103: This departs from 2026110116413708's call that the key doesn't need focus. It doesn't need it under xfwm4, which gives the window focus.
		- 20261103: The mutation checks for the 3 cases ran under the restarted xfwm4, so they need to be run again. Filed as 2026110319081175.
	- Verified: 20261103. The old script, with only the new check added, failed it, with the restarted xfwm4 on the display. The new one passed alone at load 10 to 13, and 4 runs side by side at load 25 to 52. Its window logs show the back case put back, the moved case's look after its move dropping the herd, and the resized case dropping it at the resize. Without the focus, the moved case's look waited for good and the case passed on that alone. The quick gate, scripts, and docs checks pass.
	- Swept: Every xfwm4 start in `cicd`. gui-headless.bash's fOnX and demo-video.py already drop SESSION_MANAGER, and dlgtie, startsize, and allocs start xfwm4 through gui-headless.bash. Every `xdotool windowmove` in `cicd`. idleother's also runs without a window manager, but only moves a window out from under another, and nothing there waits on the window to see the move. demo-video.py's run under xfwm4.
	- Branch: rnd1104
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/herdback/run.bash` (deqx1), changed, with the new "no window manager came back for the cases with none" check.
	- Closed: 20261103-190900

- SGR 21 turns bold off instead of drawing a double underline
	- ID: 2026110220554102
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261102-205541
	- Closed: 20261103-171842
	- Opened by: CC
	- Parent ID: 2026102511131401
	- Target OS: All
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- In SilkTerm, run `printf '\e[21mdouble\e[0m\n'`.
	- Incorrect behavior: There's no underline, and SGR 21 also turns bold off.
	- Expected behavior: A double underline, as ECMA-48, xterm, and GNOME Terminal have it.
	- Reproduced: Yes, 20261102, on b23: drawn without a line.
	- Actual cause: vte 0.15, the engine's parser, hands 21 over as "cancel bold", and the engine took bold off, as Alacritty does.
	- Notes:
		- 20261102: A fix needs a patched vte, beside the engine fork that's already patched in. Or leave it, since programs get double underline through `4:2`.
		- 20261103: No vte patch is needed. vte sends "cancel bold" for 21 and nothing else, so the engine fork can read it as a double underline.
	- Actual effort: Low
	- Decisions:
		- 20261103: It was fixed in the engine fork rather than a patched vte, so the patched crates stay at 3.
		- 20261103: SGR 21 leaves bold as it was, as in xterm, kitty, and WezTerm. A program that sends 21 to mean "bold off" now gets a double underline. SGR 22 still turns bold off.
	- Actual fix: SGR 21 sets a double underline, in place of any other underline style, and leaves bold alone. It draws as `4:2` does.
	- Swept: vte's SGR table, where only 21 gives "cancel bold" and 22 still gives "cancel bold and dim". The engine's attribute handling, the only reader of either. The pane's underline styles read the engine's double underline flag, whichever code set it. No doc says what 21 does. The comment on desqy that said 21 is "not bold" goes with the test.
	- Verified: 20261103, the fork's terminal tests, and the backlog quick run (fmt, clippy, tests, scripts, docs) with the lock on the fork commit.
	- Branch: rnd1104, and fork `scroll-ledger-0.26.0`.
	- Commit: 9fdde7c (test), fork 65dbcd81. Cargo.lock moves only the fork's commit.
	- Test case: `sgr_21_double_underlines_and_keeps_bold` (detxz), and the fork test of the same name. Both fail without the fix and pass with it.
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: detxz checks the cell flags the drawing reads, and the underline draws as `4:2` does.

- Wayland: Settings isn't tied to the terminal window
	- ID: 2026110118260314
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
		- Open Settings on a real Wayland desktop, GNOME and KDE if there are both. It should stay above the terminal, and not make a taskbar or alt+tab entry of its own where that desktop folds a dialog into its parent's.
	- Needs hand testing: No. A look on GNOME or KDE under Wayland is still welcome, but the taskbar and alt+tab entry is each desktop's own call once the parent is set.
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261101-182603
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026103010083402, 2026110317323442
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: headless sway 1.10.1
	- Incorrect behavior: On native Wayland Settings and About are toplevels of their own, with their own taskbar and alt+tab entries, and can go behind the terminal.
	- Expected behavior: The same as on X11, per 2026103010083402.
	- Reproduced: 20261103, on headless sway. Settings came up tiled beside the terminal, as a window of its own, rather than floating over it as a dialog.
	- Possible cause: winit 0.30 doesn't have a parent for a Wayland window. xdg-shell has `set_parent` for this, so it needs a winit change or a call on the raw surface.
	- Actual cause: winit 0.30 doesn't have a parent for a Wayland window, so the dialog never named one.
	- Actual fix: Each dialog's xdg_toplevel names the terminal's as its parent, on winit's own connection, before the dialog first draws. winit 0.30.13 hands out both toplevels.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261103: The call goes on winit's toplevel rather than into a winit fork. It's one request on the connection, as monitor.rs already reads winit's state there.
		- 20261103: There isn't a modal hint yet. Wayland's is the staging xdg-dialog protocol, which needs its global bound from the registry. That's 2026110317323442.
		- 20261103: Taskbar and alt+tab entries are each desktop's call on Wayland, without any state a client can set the way X11's skip hints do. The parent is all a client can give, so that part is left to the hand test.
	- Verified: 20261103. dlgwl passes 6 of 6 checks, and fails 3 with the parent call taken out: no set_parent on the wire, and the dialog tiled rather than floating, which fails its focus check too. dlgtie still passes 13 of 13 on X11. The quick gate, all 5 areas, plus clippy for Windows and macOS, pass.
		- Swept: About, the notices, and the close question are made by the same code, so they get the parent too. A notice over Settings names Settings. Off Wayland the toplevels are None and nothing is sent.
	- Branch: rnd1104
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/dlgwl/run.bash` (detyk).
	- Acceptance signoff: Self-closed: xdg-shell set_parent is the only tie Wayland gives a dialog, and dlgwl (detyk) shows it sent, with sway floating Settings over the terminal and giving it focus. It fails without the fix.
	- Closed: 20261104-013900

- The private Mac build prints empty sizes and 5 `stat` errors on b26
	- ID: 2026102811082478
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Opened: 20261028-110824
	- Opened by: CC
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Test environment: b26, through the private runner
	- Steps to reproduce: A full run with stage 6, or the private runner's `mac` job on b26.
	- Incorrect behavior: "stat: invalid option -- '%'" 5 times, then "bytes: x86_64 , arm64 , universal , zip , dmg" with no numbers.
	- Expected behavior: The 5 sizes in bytes.
	- Reproduced: 20261028, in the full run at 64f3584.
	- Possible cause: `fSize` in silkterm-private `macos/build.bash` calls `stat -f%z`, the BSD form. The `stat` first on PATH there is GNU, which wants `-c%s`.
	- Severity: Low
	- Actual cause: It was as guessed. On b26 the login PATH puts Homebrew's GNU coreutils (`gnubin`) ahead of `/usr/bin`, so `stat` is GNU's.
	- Actual fix: `fSize` counts bytes with `wc -c`, which gives the same count from GNU or BSD, and drops the padding BSD's `wc` adds. It's now with the other helpers at the top of the script.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261103: `wc -c` rather than a fixed `/usr/bin/stat`, so the line works whichever tools come first on PATH, on b26 and on vmKt6m as mactest.
	- Swept: the rest of `macos/build.bash` and the private `cicd/run.bash` for other calls that differ between GNU and BSD. None were found. `stat` appeared only in `fSize`.
	- Verified: 20261103. On b26, under bash 3.2 and Homebrew's bash 5.3 with the build's PATH, `fSize` gave the same sizes as `/usr/bin/stat -f%z`, and with only `/usr/bin` on PATH it stripped BSD wc's padding. detz1 passes, and fails on the old `fSize`.
	- Branch: silkterm-private `rnd1104`
	- Commit: silkterm-private 34c9833
	- Test case: silkterm-private `cicd/tests/macsize/run.bash` (detz1), run by hand like dehx0.
	- Closed: 20261103-173834

- Help|About: "Acceleration" shows as "Unknown"
	- ID: 2026102807384203
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261028-073842
	- Opened by: JC
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Reproduced: The startup line on b23's X11 desktop reads `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti/PCIe/SSE2 [Gl / Other]`.
	- Actual cause: On X11 the window draws through GL. wgpu's GL backend can only tell integrated and software chips apart by name, and calls everything else `Other`. About mapped `Other` to "Unknown". `--about` queries Vulkan, so it said "Hardware (discrete GPU)" on the same box.
	- Actual fix: An adapter of type `Other` reads as "Hardware (GPU)". Any adapter with a software name, from the list the performance rating already uses, reads as "Software (CPU)" whatever type it gives.
	- Decisions:
		- It reads "Hardware (GPU)" without a kind, since GL doesn't say whether the card is discrete. wgpu's own note says `Other` there is most likely a discrete card. The rest of the program already treats `Other` as a card.
		- The software name check applies to every type, so About agrees with the rating on remote and basic display drivers.
	- Swept: The other `device_type` checks in gfx.rs (`Drawn::of`, the refusal stand-in, the fallback) already count `Other` as a card. The rating goes by `profile::software_adapter`, the same list used here.
	- Notes:
		- Pre-next-cut.
		- 20261103: `every_gpu_is_hardware_and_only_the_cpu_is_software` (dd5n5) asserted that a bare `Other` is never Hardware. It now asserts that for an `Other` with a software name. Everything else it checks is unchanged.
	- Commit: 5d1e88a
	- Test case: `a_card_on_gl_is_hardware_and_a_software_name_never_is` (detz5), which fails with the old mapping and passes with the fix.
	- Closed: 20261103-174640

- `the_scroll_record_costs_a_full_screen_program_little` failed once on the Mac runner
	- ID: 2026102113432602
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
		- 20261103: The fix is in, and passes the stand-ins here. One hosted Mac run is left, in the external testing row.
	- Needs external testing: No
	- Stand-in: 20261103: b23, the test pinned to one core while its SMT sibling copies memory in random 10 to 80 ms stretches, so the core slows and speeds up under the test without the thread waiting. It stands in for the core changing under the test rather than for the Mac itself.
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261021-134326
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026102113432600, 2026100714145220
	- Target OS: macOS
	- Test environment: GitHub macos-15, arm64, 3 cores
	- Reproduced: it failed 3 of the 7 full Mac runs to 20261022 16:04 UTC (runs 39667988647, 39709345533, 39810794398). Each time it passed when run again alone, in under a second. No failure kept its numbers.
	- Possible cause: It may be memory traffic from the tests running beside it. The test times by the thread's own CPU time, which leaves out waiting for a core but not cache misses. Keeping rows cycles 128 rows of 160 cells, so each scrolled line writes a row last touched 128 lines ago. The bare side reuses rows still in cache. On b23, on 3 pinned cores, the median was 1.02 to 1.07 alone, 1.04 to 1.07 beside 3 CPU-bound loops, and 1.06 to 1.14 beside 3 memory-bound ones, failing 2 of 10 runs there. Bare against bare under the same memory load stayed 0.98 to 1.02, so the pairing is fair and the extra cost is the kept side's. An M1's cores share an L2 per cluster, and the suite runs on all 3 cores, so it may well be more there. It wasn't confirmed on the Mac.
	- Notes:
		- The Mac's clock was ruled out. macOS reads it from `__thread_selfusage()` in mach ticks, about 42 ns on an M1, against runs of about 40 ms. An Apple forum thread reports some M1 Macs leaving out the tick conversion, about 41.7 times too small, but a constant factor cancels in a ratio.
		- The copy this test was made for cost 28 to 35% here, and the pointer check catches it without any timing at all. The 10% limit is unchanged.
		- If the Mac shows a steady gap over 10%, the options are to run this test apart from the suite, or to judge the keep cost against something the neighbors slow down as much. Neither is done yet.
	- Progress log:
		- It passed 6 Mac CI runs in a row since 20261022, against 3 failures in the 7 before. The cause was never found. It could be closed as Can't reproduce, or kept open. Mac CI runs on every push to dev, so a new failure would show its numbers.
		- 20261025: Since the 10-24 failure, 6 more Mac CI runs passed it (40118767927, 40119271523, 40145850085, 40214477949, 40218542312, 40221760659), and one was canceled.
		- 20261022: The failure text was never in the CI log. `ci-mac.bash` now prints each failed test's panic text from the first run, runs the failed tests again with their output shown, and prints every `measured:` line a test writes. The test writes its ratios and each pair's times that way, and puts the times in its failure message too.
		- 20261022: Mac CI run 39842974082 on rnd1022 passed it. The median was 1.005 over 15 pairs, from 0.766 to 1.211. Kept was above bare in 9 of 15 pairs, each by a little. The big swings were on the bare side, 24.5 against 32.0 and 23.3 against 27.7 ms, which reads more like the core or host changing than a steady keep cost. That's one run, so it isn't settled. The run failed on another test, filed on 2026102114411311.

- deqx1's first case sometimes fails "the window was herded" on a busy box
	- ID: 2026110116413708
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261101-164137
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026102807384201, 2026110315170584, 2026110318260287
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Run `cicd/tests/herdback/run.bash` a few times at a load over 20.
	- Incorrect behavior: In the first xfwm4 case the window sometimes never takes the portrait size, so it straddles the 2 outputs, and xfwm4 doesn't herd it. It happened in about 2 runs in 8 on 20261101.
	- Expected behavior: Every case starts wholly on the portrait output.
	- Possible cause: Under Xwayland the buttons can't be seen, so the look after the test's move waits for a sign the drag is over, and the test doesn't give one. A pointer move or a focus change from the test didn't end it.
	- 20261103: A lead from 2026110220294255: fDance's start check tests only that x is under 1200, while fDanceBare uses fOnPortrait, so a window across both outputs passes the start and fails later at "was herded".
	- 20261103: Giving the test a sign that the drag is over would also let deqx1's moved case watch the forget-on-move, per 2026110315170584.
	- Reproduced: 20261103, every time, with the test's first move made 3 s after the window showed rather than 1. Every case failed to start on the portrait output, and both xfwm4 cases failed "the window was herded" with the window at its launch size.
	- Actual cause: The window's first look after it shows goes ahead without a sign, and takes the size of the monitor it's on. Every later look after a move waits for a sign that the person is back at the window, since under Xwayland a drag held on the title bar can't be seen. The test moved the window 1 s after it showed, and the first look comes 0.75 s after the window is revealed. On a busy box the look sometimes came first, on the landscape output, and the move after it waited for good, so the window kept the landscape size and straddled both outputs.
		- A Shift key sent to the window, pointer motion over it, or focus moved to it from another window each ended the wait. Focusing it again while it already had focus didn't, since that isn't a change.
	- Actual fix: After each move onto the portrait output the test sends the window a Shift key, which is that sign. fDance's start check uses fOnPortrait, as fDanceBare does. The moved case gets the key after its move too, so its look runs, and the case now watches the forget-on-move.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261103: The test sends a key to the window itself rather than pointer motion. It doesn't leave a pointer over a window to count as presence in a later step, and it needs neither focus nor a window manager.
	- Verified: 20261103. With the first move made late, the old script failed the start in every case, and the new one passed all 19 checks. In 7 runs of the new one at load 18 to 30, up to 4 side by side, every case started on the portrait output, and 6 runs passed whole. The other failed only "xfwm4's window has gone from the X server", filed as 2026110318260287. With the forget-on-move taken out, the moved case now fails "stays where it was left". The quick gate passed, all 5 areas.
	- Swept: Every `xdotool windowmove` in `cicd`. idleother's runs on Xvfb, where the buttons can be seen, and doesn't wait on a look.
	- Branch: rnd1104
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/herdback/run.bash` (deqx1), changed.
	- Closed: 20261103-183632

- A launch with --config pointing elsewhere still adds shell integration to the account's own shell profiles
	- ID: 2026110314410446
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Priority: Low
	- Opened: 20261103-144104
	- Opened by: CC
	- Target OS: All
	- Test environment: b23
	- Progress log:
		- 20261103: It was seen on vmKt6m while working on 2026102807384202. A launch as collierjr made ~/.config/powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1 and its folder, with --config set to a temp file. Check whether that's wanted, or whether a launch with its own config should leave the real profiles alone.
		- 20261103: Writing the profile is by design. design.md and shell-integration.md say it goes in at launch, once, unless `shell.integration` is off, and a `--config` launch reads that setting from its own file. The profile belongs to the account rather than to a config, so a `--config` session gets the same new-tab directory as any other.
		- 20261103: What was wrong was the note of profiles written to. It was kept beside the config in use, so a `--config` launch didn't find one and put back a block the user had deleted, which the docs say never happens.
	- Actual cause:
		- The note was kept in `data_dir()`, which follows `--config`.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261103: A `--config` launch still installs, governed by that file's `shell.integration`. Skipping it would leave a `--config` user without an advertised feature, and the account's profile is shared anyway. A test launch that must not touch the account gets its own HOME.
		- 20261103: The note is always kept in the account's own data folder, as without `--config`. An older note beside a `--config` file isn't read. Only dev builds since 09-08 wrote one, never a release.
	- Actual fix:
		- The note is kept in the account's data folder whatever `--config` names. shell-integration.md says so.
	- Swept: the other `data_dir`, `cache_dir`, and `state_dir` users (the bash prompt script, wallpaper cache and history, and state.shcl) are the program's own files, which the flag is meant to keep apart. Nothing else records state about files outside SilkTerm's folders.
	- Branch: rnd1103
	- Commit: cb14f0c
	- Test case: `a_config_named_on_the_command_line_reads_the_accounts_profile_note` (detst). It failed with the note beside the config, and passes with the fix.
	- Verified: the backlog quick run, all 5 areas, and Windows-target clippy.
	- Acceptance signoff: JC, 20261103. As built, option A.
	- Closed: 20261103-145900

- herdback's window lookup and stop miss the program, since `appPid` is a subshell
	- ID: 2026110220294255
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261102-202942
	- Opened by: CC
	- Assigned to: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026110118143797, 2026102807384201
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Change both `xdotool search --pid "${appPid}" --name '^SilkTerm'` lines in `cicd/tests/herdback/run.bash` to take `--all`, and run it.
	- Incorrect behavior: Every case says the window never showed. The launch is `fX ... &`, and `fX` is a function, so `$!` is the subshell rather than SilkTerm. The lookup finds the window by its name only, and `fStopOurs` sees bash rather than the binary, so it doesn't stop anything. A window from one dance can still be up in the next.
	- Expected behavior: `appPid` is the program, so the lookup can take `--all` and each dance stops its own window.
	- Notes:
		- gui-headless.bash's `fOnX --bg` execs for the same reason.
	- Reproduced: 20261103, with `--all` on both lookups: every case said the window never showed, and 5 windows were left running until the X server went.
	- Actual cause: Each launch was a function sent to the background, so `$!` was a bash waiting on the program. The same went for xfwm4: `pgrep -P` looked under the wrong parent, the kill stopped only that bash, and xfwm4 stayed up through the cases without a window manager. Its stop check passed anyway, since it only asked about pids it never found.
	- Actual fix: `fX --bg` execs, as `fOnX --bg` does, and the program, xfwm4, and the window lookups go by it. The lookups take `--all`. Each case checks its window is gone once stopped, and stops it when it never showed. The stop of xfwm4 checks its window is gone from the X server.
	- Swept: every `$!` in `cicd` after a backgrounded function. dlgtie's `fX xterm ... &` had the same problem, so its kill of the other window stopped only a bash. Its `fX --bg` execs now, and der6f still passes. idleother's `fLaunch` puts the program itself in the background inside the function, so its `$!` was already right. gui-headless already execs.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261103: The "no window manager" cases now run without one, so the mutation checks 2026102807384201 recorded for them ran with xfwm4 still up. Filed as 2026110315170584 to run them again.
	- Verified: 20261103. The script with the exec taken out failed 6 checks, the window never showing in all 5 cases, and xfwm4's window still on the X server. With it in, all 19 checks passed in 2 runs of 3, at load 7 to 10. The third failed only "the window was herded" in the first case, at load 14, the 2026110116413708 flake. There was one window on the display, so this fix doesn't explain it. der6f passed.
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/herdback/run.bash` (deqx1), with the new "gone once stopped" and "xfwm4's window has gone" checks. `cicd/tests/dlgtie/run.bash` (der6f).
	- Branch: rnd1103
	- Closed: 20261103-151705

- The rotate test's fork count went over its limit once inside the test run folder test
	- ID: 2026102518360001
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Needs local test suite run?: The full run, `cicd/cicd.bash --backlog-run-full`, in the container, for ddazx's runs of the rotate and engine tests.
	- Severity: Low
	- Opened: 20261025-183600
	- Opened by: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026102416233803, 2026102819265198
	- Target OS: Linux
	- Test environment: b23, the full run in the container at 591a9a8 on `rnd1025b`, box load about 20
	- Steps to reproduce:
		- Run the full pipeline in the container on a busy box. The test run folder test (ddazx) runs `rotate/run.bash` with the temp dir read-only.
	- Incorrect behavior: "rotating 200 files costs a few forks beyond the files it changes" counted 366 forks beyond the files changed, limit 300, and the full run stopped there.
	- Expected behavior: The fork count stays under its limit however busy the box is, or the check counts only forks the rotate script makes.
	- Reproduced: No. `rotate/run.bash` alone passed 3 of 3 with 18 forks, limit 30, and `testdir/run.bash` passed its rotate check 3 of 3 on the host.
		- 20261028: It happened again in the full run at 852e213, with 311 forks beyond the files changed, limit 300, and the engine test's fork check failing beside it. Alone on the host it passed 3 of 3, 18 forks, limit 30.
		- 20261028: Yes, in the image with a loop of short processes on the box: 1601 forks beyond the files changed, and 145 in the engine test, limit 100.
	- Actual cause: In the container `unshare` can't make a PID namespace, so `fForkCount` fell back to the kernel's fork total in `/proc/stat`, which counts every fork on the box, even best of 5.
	- Decisions:
		- 20261028: Count in the container's own PID namespace, rather than let the container make one, such as through a looser seccomp profile, which would widen what every step in it may do.
	- Actual fix: The fallback reads the last PID of the namespace it runs in, `/proc/sys/kernel/ns_last_pid`, so in the container it counts only the container's forks. On a box where no namespace can be made it counts the box's, as before. `/proc/stat` is left for a kernel without the file.
	- Verified: 20261028. In the image under the same load, the old helper failed both checks and the new one passed both at the exact counts, 18 and 4. `rotate/run.bash` alone on the host passed 3 of 3. shellcheck, the bash style check, and `--backlog-run-quick` with all 5 areas pass.
		- Swept: both callers of `fForkCount`, the rotate and engine tests. No other test counts forks.
		- 20261028: The full run at 9eded41, in the container, passed ddazx with the rotate and engine fork checks in it. The run at 852e213 before the fix failed there.
	- Branch: rnd1029
	- Test case: The fork checks in dd5nq `cicd/tests/rotate/run.bash` and dd5nn `cicd/tests/engine/run.bash`, which ddazx runs in the container.
	- Closed: 20261028-223038

- Over ssh, the step rule from `cicd-win.ps1` comes out as 79 bell characters
	- ID: 2026102811082453
	- Type: Bug
	- Status: Done
	- Opened: 20261028-110824
	- Opened by: CC
	- Related IDs: 2026102416233808
	- Target OS: Windows
	- Test environment: b29w, through `win-remote.bash`
	- Steps to reproduce: Run `cicd-win.ps1 -BacklogRunQuick fmt` on b29w through `win-remote.bash run`, and keep the output in a file.
	- Incorrect behavior: Each rule above a step line is 79 BEL bytes (0x07) instead of the dot rule. A terminal beeps 79 times per step.
	- Expected behavior: The same 79-wide rule as `cicd.bash` prints, or a plain ASCII one where the output encoding doesn't have a dot.
	- Reproduced: 20261028, in the test run at 64f3584. The rule was 73 wide before the change and did the same.
	- Possible cause: The rule is `[char]0x2022`. Over ssh, pwsh writes through the OEM code page, 437, where the dot is byte 0x07.
	- Severity: Low
	- Actual cause: Over ssh, or into a file, pwsh encodes what it writes in the console's code page, 437 on b29w. .NET maps the dot there to 0x07, the bell. Write-Host settles its encoding at its first write.
	- Actual fix: Before any output, `cicd-win.ps1` switches output to UTF-8 when it isn't going to a console, and puts the code page back at the end, since the shell that started it shares the console. Where the switch fails and the dot can't be written, the rule is 79 dashes.
	- Decisions:
		- Only redirected output switches. A console window draws the dot already, through the wide-character call, whatever the code page.
		- UTF-8 rather than the ASCII rule as the main fix, so a log from ssh matches `cicd.bash` and native tools' UTF-8 output reads back whole.
	- Verified: 20261028. On b29w through `win-remote.bash run`, with `-BacklogRunQuick fmt`, the old script wrote 158 bell bytes and no dots, but the new one wrote 158 dots and no bell byte, and the code page read 437 again after. The new dd5nw checks fail with the switch stubbed out and pass with it. `--backlog-run-quick` with all 5 areas passed.
		- The dash fallback is unverified, since the switch never failed on b29w.
		- Swept: `cicd-win.ps1` doesn't have any other non-ASCII output. `install.ps1` and the test scripts don't print a rule.
	- Branch: rnd1029
	- Test case: `cicd/tests/cicd-win/run.bash` (dd5nw), "a rule written to a pipe is 79 dots in UTF-8".
	- Closed: 20261028-191249
